maybe a mix? Akira by that point had a bizarre idea of love in a mix of "savior" and "abuser". Maya isn't just a fucktoy that's also the same age he was when Sekai started abusing/saving him - she's him.

Maybe that's another reason why Sekai hates her so much, she could be the proof that Sekai's "love" was perceived as fucked up by him (since he wished for a different dynamic).

I disagree with this sentence. Because what happens is so far from this.
Akira we watched didn't knock up Ayane and run off with her. He was dropped to a world he knows for a limited time . He knew this from the start. He didn't even know Himawari much. Just like the very start of the game, a new world and a new daughter/niece he doesnt know.

Yet unlike the first three chapters and first half of chapter 4, even though he kind of knew this world he lives is a lie and will end one day... He actually lives a life, as well as a spineless bastard can live.

One of the most frustrating part of the first pre 0.53 was how passive and his unwillingness to take an action. We learn in the event "kyoto" the reason for his worldwiew is fear of abondonment. Losing something he dears scares him so much he can not hold something close to his heart. Thats why we see same quote "i could never leave you even if i want to" with Sekai and Niki.

In this new world, however, he learns to take and give affection, despite knowing that the rug will be pulled out from under him.

In 0.53 when he lost the daughter he learned to love, he didn't become a lifeless body he was in the beginning of the chapter 4. He accepted it and spend the last moments with Himawari while learning more about her and the world he lives.

The 0.53 update made it possible for Akira to eventually become the person we later see in Aomori.

This is why I am hopeful for the future of both the game as a story and Akira as a character.

This is probably why so many people liked it.

Okay, I've been absolutely dead wrong about all my theorycrafting I've done so far (though there is still a possibility that Nodoka's not supposed to be here), but this update has had the most transparent language in a while that's so intriguing that I'm ready to be dead wrong again:
There was one moment in particular that caught my interest, that felt just out of place enough that I decided that I needed to play this update over again (three more times) to try to read into it all. During Himawari's tearful parting, when she's wiping Akira and Ayane's memories of her, she blurts this out as a throwaway line, not really expecting anyone to know what she's talking about but more for herself:
She...misses them.
She...misses them? Why? Why would she miss them? As far as we knew up until this point, she was just a time-traveler messing with the past. If she ever wanted to see her beloved parents again, why not go back to the future? Why does she miss them so much? Where are they that she can't get back to them just by going back to the future? You might already know where I'm going with this, but hold on to this moment; we'll come back to it as we break down more moments from the update.
For starters, the fact that Himawari's pocket dimension (and by extension Himawari) exists at all means that Akira and Ayane are going to break free from Terminal23 and have Himawari, and she says so herself:
During Playthrough #3 of this update, I fully realized that the "fake" nature of Himawari's pocket dimension serves as hints of what the True Timeline is like, kinda like how when you know for a fact that someone is lying to you, you can invert some of their statements to find out what's actually going on. Akira also figured that out himself, and this moment is some of the most transparent and least ambiguous writing we've seen in a while.
So, in Himawari's fantasy of what a perfect life looks like, the family moved as far away as they could possibly get from Kumon-Mi and left everything and everyone behind, except for some long-distance contact with Sana for some reason (I'll be honest I haven't figured out why) and some very low contact with Ami under controlled circumstances. She then lives every day carefree with just her Mama and Papa making casual good-faith jabs at each other and making precious memories with each other.

So what's the reflection of this?

In the true timeline, Akira still hasn't reconciled his relationships with the greater harem or his relationship with himself, and it's made for a very unstable upbringing for Himawari, regardless of how much he clearly loves her and how much she clearly loves him. Akira's attention was constantly being pulled away from his family to all the other women in his life, and no one was ever satisfied with having only a portion of his attention (evidenced by how Himawari's dream, which is clearly the purity routes, is for each person to get the opportunity to "vacation" in their own happy ending, no strings attached, as well as a quick quip about "dad's harem" in the breakfast scene), and Himawari briefly touches on her broken home when she's getting chastised by Shiori.
"I want my family to be a family", bless her.
Akira also hasn't made peace with himself and has not corrected his corrupted understanding of love. He spends years and years feeling empty and searching for something to fill that emptiness, and the closest thing he every found was his daughter Himawari, though he never truly knew how to show his love for her (thankfully, clearly it was not sexually). He still spends every moment paranoid that the good things in life are about to be stolen from him, and that's even still the first thing he's thinking when He and Ayane get whisked away to Himawari's pocket dimension.
Granted, that's a logical conclusion to come to given all they've seen, but the fact that our Akira, the same one who will eventually break out of Terminal23 without any outside guidance immediately thought about how they could lose it all really tells us how even after he's emotionally grown, he's not prepared for his freedom from Terminal 23 and by extension created the broken household Himawari was raised in.

This was so bad, that something happened that meant that Himawari can't see her parents anymore. Something so permanent that plucking them out of their timeline into a manufactured future wasn't goo enough, that the only possible way she could see them again was joining the Megacorp of the gods (I think it's called the Shiawase Group) and subtlety messing with the timeline in the hope that Akira will come out of it a fully emotionally realized person who can be the father that Himawari wants back.
You've probably pieced together what I'm implying here, so let's piece this all together along with other theories from the thread and come up with The Greater Timeline of LiL
Akira spends most of his life getting physically or sexually abused by Nozomu and Sekai. After years and years of the most fucked up game of Good Cop/Bad Cop, Nozomu and Sekai suddenly die in an unexpected car crash. Sekai is desperately experimented on, both scientifically and pseudoscientifically with the full resources of House Tsukioka under the direction of her friend Tsubasa in a desperate attempt to keep her alive to no avail, but it does result in Sekai's soul being bound to the world and the beginning of her ascendancy to godhood. As Akira is reeling and directionless in his newfound freedom, he makes a wish of uknown wording that result in Maya coming into his life. The wording of his wish could be anything from "Keeping Sekai's memory alive" or "I wish someone could love me like Her." Maya falls in love with him, but it doesn't help him at all, as Akira sinks further and further into depression. In desperation, Maya somehow makes a wish that defies the expected metaphysics of the multiverse, phrased something along the lines of "I wish everyone loves him as much as he loves me". She makes this wish/pact with a god, and curiously, it seems to be the only god she knows of. Maya only ever talks about God (singular) and never the gods (plural), so what kind of god could make a wish that so fundamentally changes the nature of the world, unless it's the god of the world itself: Sekai, god of Terminal23. Sekai fulfills Maya's wish, but not in the way she wanted and even swapped her place with Ami as Akira's main partner. What follows is eons of a predatory orgy that the gods just can't figure out how to stop until one cycle the true Akira re-emerged. Akira eventually unravels the mystery of Terminal23 and breaks the timeloop, setting everyone free...who still all want his dick. He has Himawari with Ayane, and Himawari grows up in the middle of a chaotic harem as everyone constantly fights and bickers over Akira while he tries and fails to keep the peace while being spread thin over so many people. After 15 years of this, he's mentally and emotionally exhausted with all of his relationships broken, just as lost and directionless as when his abusers first died. Something with some degree of finality happens. Perhaps it's a relapse into his taste for younger girls, or perhaps it's a particularly brutal argument with Ayane or Himawari, but one day, mirroring the start of Himawari's pocket dimension, she returned home from school, immediately launching into a prepared speech about dropping out of school to keep an eye on her father, when she found his stone-cold corpse hanging in the living room. In grief, she searched for any possible way she could time travel until she contacted the Shiawase Group (or whatever the Megacorp of the gods is called) and joined as a custodian with the express intention of meddling with the timeline in hopes of producing a different result, leading right to where we are now in the story.
In any rate, 10/10 update. Absolutely loved every part of it, and I'm really bummed that it's gonna be a long while before we see Himawari again. The single cutest thing she did was when she thought Geoffrey was ringing the doorbell, she went:

Tying it All Together
Akira spends most of his life getting physically or sexually abused by Nozomu and Sekai. After years and years of the most fucked up game of Good Cop/Bad Cop, Nozomu and Sekai suddenly die in an unexpected car crash. Sekai is desperately experimented on, both scientifically and pseudoscientifically with the full resources of House Tsukioka under the direction of her friend Tsubasa in a desperate attempt to keep her alive to no avail, but it does result in Sekai's soul being bound to the world and the beginning of her ascendancy to godhood. As Akira is reeling and directionless in his newfound freedom, he makes a wish of uknown wording that result in Maya coming into his life. The wording of his wish could be anything from "Keeping Sekai's memory alive" or "I wish someone could love me like Her." Maya falls in love with him, but it doesn't help him at all, as Akira sinks further and further into depression. In desperation, Maya somehow makes a wish that defies the expected metaphysics of the multiverse, phrased something along the lines of "I wish everyone loves him as much as he loves me". She makes this wish/pact with a god, and curiously, it seems to be the only god she knows of. Maya only ever talks about God (singular) and never the gods (plural), so what kind of god could make a wish that so fundamentally changes the nature of the world, unless it's the god of the world itself: Sekai, god of Terminal23. Sekai fulfills Maya's wish, but not in the way she wanted and even swapped her place with Ami as Akira's main partner. What follows is eons of a predatory orgy that the gods just can't figure out how to stop until one cycle the true Akira re-emerged. Akira eventually unravels the mystery of Terminal23 and breaks the timeloop, setting everyone free...who still all want his dick. He has Himawari with Ayane, and Himawari grows up in the middle of a chaotic harem as everyone constantly fights and bickers over Akira while he tries and fails to keep the peace while being spread thin over so many people. After 15 years of this, he's mentally and emotionally exhausted with all of his relationships broken, just as lost and directionless as when his abusers first died. Something with some degree of finality happens. Perhaps it's a relapse into his taste for younger girls, or perhaps it's a particularly brutal argument with Ayane or Himawari, but one day, mirroring the start of Himawari's pocket dimension, she returned home from school, immediately launching into a prepared speech about dropping out of school to keep an eye on her father, when she found his stone-cold corpse hanging in the living room. In grief, she searched for any possible way she could time travel until she contacted the Shiawase Group (or whatever the Megacorp of the gods is called) and joined as a custodian with the express intention of meddling with the timeline in hopes of producing a different result, leading right to where we are now in the story.
In any rate, 10/10 update. Absolutely loved every part of it, and I'm really bummed that it's gonna be a long while before we see Himawari again. The single cutest thing she did was when she thought Geoffrey was ringing the doorbell, she went:
Spoiler:
Hima-Chan
Also, Adult Sana is hilarious

Sekai is desperately experimented on, both scientifically and pseudoscientifically with the full resources of House Tsukioka under the direction of her friend Tsubasa in a desperate attempt to keep her alive to no avail, but it does result in Sekai's soul being bound to the world and the beginning of her ascendancy to godhood. As Akira is reeling and directionless in his newfound freedom, he makes a wish of uknown wording that result in Maya coming into his life. The wording of his wish could be anything from "Keeping Sekai's memory alive" or "I wish someone could love me like Her." Maya falls in love with him, but it doesn't help him at all, as Akira sinks further and further into depression. In desperation, Maya somehow makes a wish that defies the expected metaphysics of the multiverse, phrased something along the lines of "I wish everyone loves him as much as he loves me". She makes this wish/pact with a god, and curiously, it seems to be the only god she knows of. Maya only ever talks about God (singular) and never the gods (plural), so what kind of god could make a wish that so fundamentally changes the nature of the world, unless it's the god of the world itself: Sekai, god of Terminal23. Sekai fulfills Maya's wish, but not in the way she wanted and even swapped her place with Ami as Akira's main partner. What follows is eons of a predatory orgy that the gods just can't figure out how to stop until one cycle the true Akira re-emerged. Akira eventually unravels the mystery of Terminal23 and breaks the timeloop, setting everyone free...who still all want his dick. He has Himawari with Ayane, and Himawari grows up in the middle of a chaotic harem as everyone constantly fights and bickers over Akira while he tries and fails to keep the peace while being spread thin over so many people. After 15 years of this, he's mentally and emotionally exhausted with all of his relationships broken, just as lost and directionless as when his abusers first died. Something with some degree of finality happens. Perhaps it's a relapse into his taste for younger girls, or perhaps it's a particularly brutal argument with Ayane or Himawari, but one day, mirroring the start of Himawari's pocket dimension, she returned home from school, immediately launching into a prepared speech about dropping out of school to keep an eye on her father, when she found his stone-cold corpse hanging in the living room. In grief, she searched for any possible way she could time travel until she contacted the Shiawase Group (or whatever the Megacorp of the gods is called) and joined as a custodian with the express intention of meddling with the timeline in hopes of producing a different result, leading right to where we are now in the story.

When he goes back to the future, history is the same, and no one could have guessed that Beethoven was a timetraveler. When she views Sensei's world through her phone app, it sounds like real-time streaming rather than some sort of video on demand thing.

So Sensei's present must have some special meaning in her own timeline as well, and I think Shiori explains why: her world is one of many where time runs in parallel to Sensei's world.

Shiori is telling Himawari that she's at risk because her own world is among the ones now threatened. And just to be clear, that's the only reason she might be erased - if she's caught by the corporation, they'll only delete the relevant parts of her memory.

So I think Himawari "time travels" only in the sense that it's 2036 in her world and she goes back to 2020 when she comes to Sensei's world. But she doesn't choose when exactly she shows up, the two worlds are synchronized so that time flows at the same rate in each. They just don't line up in terms of calendar year because Himawari's world either doesn't reset or resets far less often.

There's one thing I can't explain, though: if time in Himawari's world runs in parallel to Sensei's world at the same rate, she should have aged 5+ years over the course of the game, but by all accounts she has always looked like a 15-year-old girl. Sensei's world isn't supposed to be special for her in any way, so would that mean she can travel into the past in any world? What about her own?


About the scarf specifically: Alt Maya Prime's scarf had been around forever, it's well-worn, has a distinct smell, etc. The scarf Himawari sold to Sensei looked brand new from the factory. I guess Himawari's custodial powers might have let her reset it to its original condition, but is that really any different from using an exact replica?

spoilers.title: Bootstrap scarf and Himawari's plan
spoilers.html:
This entire part is trying to tie the idea of a bootstrap to Maya's scarf, and speculating on Himawari being able to actually timetravel inside the simulation. At the end of the day, it's all speculation though.

Himawari's officially gone for now, and what the hell was her plan anyway? From what I get, there was none? She was just trying to get information and prevent Akira and Ayane from being reset, from what I can tell. And maybe she was responsible for Maya's eventual demise (not on purpose), but from her bootstrap scarf.

I don't think anyone has talked about this either, so let's talk about it.

Himawari seems to not have joined from the start, I don't think, otherwise she'd have likely been spotted by now - I think it's likely she started working there because of our Akira, which is hers as well. So, how Himawari intended to get more information that was unable to be acquired by the company over so long? My guess is that she tried investigating both Ami and Maya. The Ami part I'm unsure about because I don't have evidence about it for now, but we can safely assumed that she tried talking to her a couple of times and had Shiori torture her for info as well.

But, regarding Maya, my guess was that the whole thing had to do with the scarf. And since the scarf resulted in nothing as of this reset, my guess was that it was already used. For this to work, people have to understand what a "bootstrap paradox" is. This paradox happens when an object has no discernible point of origin, due to timetravel.

A Doctor Who example of this was that a timetraveler loved Beethoven's music, so they go back in the past to meet him. But when they arrive, no one has ever heard of him - and the timetraveler despairs at the idea of a world without his favorite composer. Thus, he calls himself Beethoven, and publishes all of his compositions as if he was Beethoven himself. When he goes back to the future, history is the same, and no one could have guessed that Beethoven was a timetraveler. But then, the question remains: who actually wrote the compositions in the first place? This is called bootstrap paradox.

posts.content_html_raw:
This is a picture posted by X acount "AreYouHappyHere" in February this year, "if a wish could wish what would it wish".

I think it is a diagram of Wishing Well. Here are my guesses of what this picture means. Most of them may not be correct, I just want to share.

The outermost area represents the "worlds of wishes," where time can loop and the worlds themselves can die. The space between might be the "real worlds" where people like Himawari live and the timeline progresses linearly. The center could be the "true" real world Himawari referred to, a place that blinds any real person who enters it (is this the library from the "Mother's Milk" event?).

The black cluster has a noticeable protrusion extending into the space between the two circles. This might mean that gods can enter the real worlds to affect them.
The blue cluster spills out slightly beyond the outer circle in a few places. This could suggest that people from the real worlds, like Himawari and Shiori, can also be chosen by the "Company."

The colorful stars represent individual "wish worlds." Ami has a world where Sekai is still alive and Maya doesn't exist. She killed Nodoka there. Himawari got her Aomori. Maya obtained our Komon-mi, though the outcome wasn't good. As for Ayane, even Himawari doesn't know what Ayane's wish was. Sekai's wish world has no connection to the black cluster. We don't know what this implies, but it might be why Ami is so special.

In this diagram, Komon-mi, represented by the green star, is stuck between the wish worlds and the real worlds because of Maya. Perhaps this is what is meant by "two parts". And why strange things continue happen.

Ami's and Himawari's wish worlds are not touching the circle like the other 23 circular wish worlds, which might be normal. However, Sekai's and Ayane's are touching the circle. This probably means something important.
There is also one wish world that isn't connected to the black cluster like the others. I don't know why or what it means.

What does "Press Play" mean?

What Chika is wearing is "Jirai", it's a new fashion trend in Japan where you wear clothes that make you look Cute and Edgy at the same time, it's mostly pink and black colors.
Wearing Jirai is supposed to symbolize that you're cute and dangerous, kind of like how being "blonde" in Japan makes you a delinquent.

Adding to the comment, Jirai is a genre highly related to Menhera. It is short for 'Mental Health' and is usually referred to girls who are mentally unwell in Japanese. I would've said Chika's pretty self-aware in her choice of clothing but Jirai is basically something Menhera girls embrace fully themselves, so it's no surprise here. She really is going full Menhera.

Okay so I just played through .52 and .53 and what can I say that hasn't already been said. Not really any spoilers in this post but Ill mark it for politeness

0.52 I was definitely struggling to read just from LiL fatigue. Akira has just been increasingly unlikable and I found myself just not giving a shit about him especially after the Niki thing an update before, this dude was a lost cause in my head.

0.53 Finally some good fucking food. The writing in chapter 4 I think in general, super mid, this update though I literally couldn't put it down. Not just because it was wholesome but because I think it was some really good character writing for Akira. The Lore has finally been explained by the author in a more clear way, which some people might not like because its in your face but come on now, its not like idk Umineko. Just because this VN has more words than umineko does not an umineko make. Aside from that this update gave me some hope (no pun intended) that this POS character can have "some" redemption. Completely removed from personal morals, that's what I wanted from this character since reading from like idk 0.12. Its funny because there was a line Akira thinks that was something like "why else would you read this if im not suffering" and outloud I said "because I wanna see you be better a human being wtf". Literally all of his problems are so solvable. Regardless this update was great, music, story, writing all great.

The Bootstrap Paradox idea lines up too well not to be true. The scarf is the starting gun, and we'll be seeing more objects in the future. Maybe the endgame to fixing the world is getting Maya to realize/admit the wish nature of herself and the world to Akira, and Himawari saw that it could only happen by getting Maya to open back up.
Click to expand...
For me, this is one scary, beautiful, and sorrowful idea all at once bundled together. Now that we know how Kumon-mi came to be, maybe the only way to escape its confine really isn't about making it through custodians, dodging gods' poking, and doing some overly complicated timey wimey shit. Maybe it really comes to Maya finally being ready to let go, to relinquish her wish and crumble those impossible walls, and to say goodbye to her creator/lover one last time so that he may move on. It's like what you'd have done with your coping mechanism imaginary friend once you've regained your footing and are ready to move forward.

(though it technically might not work that way as the Maya Prime we come to know wasn't the one that wished Kumon-mi into existence as I understand, but I'd love to have my heart stabbed one more time before finally being done with LiL)

I have a tinfoil prediction to share.

By clicking on the spoiler below, the reader accepts all risks associated with exposure to dangerously stupid theories and acknowledges that aramaug is not liable for any resulting loss of IQ.
I think Maya Prime is back.



As I'm sure everyone remembers, this was a favorite phrase of Maya Prime. A couple examples (there are a ton more):


New Maya never said anything like this spontaneously. She recently starting calling him disgusting, but only after he told her it was something Maya Prime did.

There's no real feeling behind it and it's always in reference to Maya Prime. She certainly hasn't adopted Maya Prime's signature look of disdain. In fact, I skimmed through a bunch of events and struggled to find examples of her showing similar emotions in any context - at the very least, it's exceedingly rare.

* Technically I think it's a Maya that has the memories of both Maya Prime and New Maya. There's a few ways that could be true, but the most likely is that Maya Prime absorbed New Maya just like Himawari did with her "solar panel".

This line is only a small part of why I believe it's her. I think Maya Prime's return explains some of the cryptic clues surrounding New Maya's death in 0.52, and because of that I was on the lookout for anything suspicious in 0.53. I still intend to write about the events of 0.52, but that'll take a lot of work and I decided I didn't want to wait until then to share this.

posts.content_html_raw:
Preface: I'm under the impression that even the people critical of this game have positive thoughts about this update, so I'm not expecting anyone to agree with what I have to say here, but I needed to get it out of my system.

1- The first half was one of the cringiest birthing/nuclear family propaganda I've ever seen, how did this VN go from being about how sexual abuse damages people beyond repair to "having a tradwife and a child fixes all problems, even for a predator". There isn't even an argument that can be made about narrative intention here since the only unfortunate thing about this situation is that it ended too soon. Sel genuinely believes this is a "good ending" for Akira that would have worked. And don't get me started on how weird it is for Ayane to be completely fine with suddenly being in a life where she doesn't have contact with any of her friends, like can't you at least write her being somewhat lonely? These characters have stopped feeling human a long time ago. Himawari knows about what her dad does and how she was born, and instead of reacting like any human being would (with disgust, disbelief, and conflicting feelings), she only has positive things to say about Akira and his relationship with Ayane. Actually disgusting writing.

2- Sel can drop hundreds of lines saying this but he will never convince me about the whole "Maya is a fake delusion while Ami is real" thing, that's just Ami/Sekai propaganda. He's either baiting really hard and gonna flip it on its head eventually, or he's actually the most shallow writer to ever exist since he's clearly just trying to spite Maya fans. I don't know if people here realize this, but if Maya is actually fake that would mean that Akira has no real world victims at all, and we're already lowering his accountability for the Kumon Mi actions (especially with the horrible implications about his true age), are we heading towards a point where Akira has actually never done anything wrong? Also, Himawari herself said that if anyone was a faker/shapeshifter, it would be Ami and Niki, she never brought up Maya. Like, come on. This just feels like an malicious attack on the people who actually took this narrative seriously and tried to make sense of it by following the clues, we are being punished for thinking critically about the story and trying to analyze it instead of "feeling" it or whatever Sel whines about all the time.

3- The entire lore of this story lost all of its aura; the way these reveals are being dropped in such a boring fashion, and the really dry irony-poisoned American humor that's shoved into every line no matter the context or tone kill any existential horror that used to be present before. I actually can't believe that Sel somehow managed to make LiL's lore feel so poorly thought out and shallow by fucking up the exposition so bad. Even the most amateurish writers can do better than that.

4- I deeply despise that even after promising Maya he would do his best to get her back, he hasn't done ANYTHING to progress in this world or find out more information, yet the implication with this update seems to be that he will do that for Himawari's sake. I can almost imagine Sel smirking to himself at the thought of knocking down Maya fans and saying "See, the daughter's pure love moves him in ways Maya's lustful fake love never could".

5- And of course, the most predictable thing ended up happening at the end with them getting their memories erased and returning to the status quo, because we can't ever have anything destabilize the precious sandbox structure that Sel is too comfortable writing, it happened with the previous timeline hopping update and I just knew it would happen here again. And yeah, it's not 100% erasure since they still retain hints of information, but we all know this will not lead to any substantial progress until many years later. Absolute garbage.

posts.content_html_raw:
I do concur with the criticism that Akira and Ayane fit into the pocket dimension too naturally. Though, giving some thought into it, I think it's a reflection of how horny everyone naturally gets in Kumon-mi. Maybe it's a consequence of the world having its own mind. Kumon-mi's more horny, Himawari's more wholesome, they pull their strings on the cast to shove them around mentally.

That being said. What makes it all so easy to accept to them is how simple happiness could be. If you asked Akira before 0.53 what happiness is, he probably would say something about wanting Maya back and everything. Even if he did get Maya back, he still has 2 yanderes to deal with, having to live with the consequence of grooming his students into someone unrecognizable, forever emotionally maiming people who loved him, unrequited; the world itself doing tricks on him. He probably would be happy to weather the storm with Maya, but it isn't like there isn't anything to worry about.

In contrast, Himawari's pocket dimension literally has nothing for him to be concerned with. Turns out, you really could live with running around from all of your problems and a fresh start. A click, and everything dragging you down is gone. You have no reason to start new problems, no reason to go back to old ones (That's why he refused to return to Kumon-mi), so why don't you just...live with it? Indulge in it? You've been given a second chance. Heck, you even get to experience the pure familial love that you missed out on, why isn't that right to you? Having lived through the midst of Lessons in Love, who knew life could be so simple?

That's why I don't think it's a cliche-themed update. It isn't just 'hurr durr trad family' on its own, but a life that Akira didn't even know he wanted. It showed him that there is a place and time somewhere in the far future of possibilities where he'll be away from his problems, isn't that the point of the update instead?

I seriously don't get why some people have such a strong reaction about Maya's provenance. Does it really matter whether she crawled out of a womb or from wherever wishes come from? She is exactly as real in either case, in my opinion.
Click to expand...
A direct comparison for the newest piece of Maya lore is Maria from Silent Hill 2.
Both characters are physical manifestations of the main characters' darkest desires. Sensei's love for the loli created Maya and James' sexual frustration from having a dying wife that he murdered, created Maria. They both serve as reminders of the fucked up parts of those characters. And only when they embrace, acknowledge and move on from these fucked up parts of themselves, do they heal. But if they continue on to wallow in self pity with said reminders, do they continue the cycle. If you say fuck Maria, you get the good ending and are able to leave Silent Hill. But if James embraces Maria, then he's doomed to repeat the cycle and stays stuck in Silent Hill. Sensei doesn't fall in love with a real girl. He falls in love with the idea of his perfect girl(that so just happens to be a wizard). Somebody just as broken as him, somebody that will love him no matter what, despite his abhorrent flaws. And once he got to act on his deepest desire, is when everything is taken away from him and he rejects it. It's most akin to a child asking for a toy for Christmas, only to get it, and kick it to the curb a few weeks later. Sensei doesn't love Maya the "person." He loves Maya the idea. It's the same thing with Sekai in the reset. He gets to experience a reality where, he and Sekai ran away together, only to be depressed when he gets everything he wanted. (Which now makes me think there are multiple Ami's and Stabby Ami or another Ami, created something similar to Himawari's pocket dimension.) Maya's only purpose is to remind Akira that he's a spineless, child diddling, piece of shit; which Nu-Maya reminds him of in one of her events (I forgot which one it is.) And once he goes off the beaten path of being an incestuous, child diddling, piece of shit, which is Maya's only purpose to remind him of, does he become a better person.

TLDR: No Maya = Better Akira
Addon: I'm really starting to notice a lot of similarities between Silent Hill 2 and Lessons in Love.

Ami sort of talks about this when Niki asks her about her mother and she talks about how Sekai had a unique way of thinking and could sway with her words so easily.

I'm not disregarding the infection idea mind, I can see it, but I was pondering Futaba's crashouts myself earlier so I wanted a reason to think out loud lol

chikipiki said:
We know Nao was born from a wish. And she has both Ami and Maya's eyes and the game made a big deal about it. What do u guys think?
Click to expand...
A lot of speculation to unpack.
Well, let's start from the wish, and some of what I say won't have pictures because I ran over the limit. During "Il Cervo", Kaori says that she traded her gold star for Nao-chan, which I take to mean that if Nao-chan is a wish, she's Kaori's. Now, we know that wishes go to another version of you that didn't wish for them. That would mean that Kaori from another reality made some sort of wish that granted this Kaori Nao-chan.

A Kaori from another reality could have made a wish related to her car accident, maybe "I want to live" or "I want to have a family", I have no idea. That also doesn't exactly fit with Nao-chan being sent to them:
This would imply Nao-chan was sent to help Akira, even though she's Kaori's wish? There's also the possibility that she is Kaori's wish, but from an older version of Kaori that wants to help Akira for some reason. Another thing to keep in mind is that the whole "we're sending her to you" could be gods making a pact with the Wishing Kaori, but then we have Pareidolia saying he doesn't know what she is, and Nao-chan actively rejecting Sekai as well.
Sekaori considers Nao-chan not a real girl, cause yeah, obviously she's not. But she doesn't seem to be involved with her either. I also added a bit from Sekaori talking about Maya cause under the light of this being her world, it's ironic that Sekai's complaining she doesn't move on. I think Sekai has also talked about Maya not being real, but I don't recall. Ami certainly has (implied), so I'd assume Sekai knows as well.

Since we're already on Maya, we have the whole thing with Nao-chan trying to help her. And when she does, even Moyo and Maya2 show up. Also, there is a reference to a lake, which I assume is the lake of the "house by the lake" on TERMINAL 22, more on that later.


now that we have confirmed TERMINAL 23 is Maya's wish, this conversation makes even more sense. She puts Maya to live her wish from the perspective of Akira, but she keeps focusing on Akira and how to get out, and Nao-chan explains that this is the wrong approach. She's showing her these things from his perspective because she wants her to understand the reality of HER WISH. This is about Maya being able to understand herself, not Akira. I'd assume that by realizing she's the one responsible for this wish, she may control it to some extent - but New Maya rejects the experience and fails the help.

Back to Nao-chan, she calls Akira her father. Which I think is very important now that we have also confirmed that Akira can only be healed by fatherhood. She states that the world is broken because of Pareidolia (and the other gods) not him, so he should stop blaming himself. She also says she's there to be his miracle.


At the end of the day, Himawari fails because she did not have enough power to begin with. She interfered as well as she could but that was very limited from the start. To be able to change the outcome for the better, they need Maya, Ami, and Nao-chan. The possible allies: Nodoka, Tsubasa and the rooftop squad. While we also have the wildcards: Sekai, the makeshift gods and Shiori.

Well, I kept thinking to myself, just how exactly can Nao-chan be a miracle and on whose plan? One other moment I think is relevant is just before Akira confronts Pareidolia in Kaori's body, when Nao-chan sends him to Terminal 22. By the way, when he checks his phone it's "22:23", good one, Selebus. But, back to it, she sends him to the house by the lake to meet Miu, to what is conceivably his original Terminal. She says so "You didn't blackout, you went home".

Many people have stated that Terminal 23 is not Akira's terminal, and while I'm not 100% convinced it is 22, let's think a bit about the implications. If Nao-chan can just send him to 22, just as Himawari sent him to her pocket dimension, escaping 23 doesn't seem that impossible of an end goal. I mean, we all know the game will end with interdimensional travel, but my point here is that Nao-chan sends him to a point in time of 22 before Sekai was born.

Himawari states that most universes go for a LONG time before they're reset, 23 is just bizarre being reset so often. Well, what if 22 does go for much longer, and Nao-chan just sent him there at the wrong point in time? Or wrong cycle? What if 22 also loops around Yuu and in one loop he stays with Miu(which we saw happening), then in another he stays with Saki, then with Kyoko?

Well, back to Nao-chan's ultimate purpose here, there is an early event where Akira clearly states the purpose of the game and his salvation while looking at her. And then he says that maybe she is the visual representation of the concept of fatherhood.

i don't that that's exactly it, but Nao-chan is half Maya and half Ami. She's also TEMPLATE 9. Well, a template of what? Neither the gods nor Sekai seem to understand what she is, and all the while she's half something that shouldn't exist (Maya), and the other half something that they can't touch (Ami).
Depressingly, I don't think we've advanced much in the understanding of Nao-chan. But from this research maybe someone can go further, or we just have to wait and see.

To be able to change the outcome for the better, they need Maya, Ami, and Nao-chan. The possible allies: Nodoka, Tsubasa and the rooftop squad. While we also have the wildcards: Sekai, the makeshift gods and Shiori.
Well, I kept thinking to myself, just how exactly can Nao-chan be a miracle and on whose plan? One other moment I think is relevant is just before Akira confronts Pareidolia in Kaori's body, when Nao-chan sends him to Terminal 22. By the way, when he checks his phone it's "22:23", good one, Selebus. But, back to it, she sends him to the house by the lake to meet Miu, to what is conceivably his original Terminal. She says so "You didn't blackout, you went home".
Many people have stated that Terminal 23 is not Akira's terminal, and while I'm not 100% convinced it is 22, let's think a bit about the implications. If Nao-chan can just send him to 22, just as Himawari sent him to her pocket dimension, escaping 23 doesn't seem that impossible of an end goal. I mean, we all know the game will end with interdimensional travel, but my point here is that Nao-chan sends him to a point in time of 22 before Sekai was born.
Himawari states that most universes go for a LONG time before they're reset, 23 is just bizarre being reset so often. Well, what if 22 does go for much longer, and Nao-chan just sent him there at the wrong point in time? Or wrong cycle? What if 22 also loops around Yuu and in one loop he stays with Miu(which we saw happening), then in another he stays with Saki, then with Kyoko?
Well, back to Nao-chan's ultimate purpose here, there is an early event where Akira clearly states the purpose of the game and his salvation while looking at her. And then he says that maybe she is the visual representation of the concept of fatherhood.

Neither the gods nor Sekai seem to understand what she is, and all the while she's half something that shouldn't exist (Maya), and the other half something that they can't touch (Ami).

Just want to drop my own thoughts in on .53, while Aramaug, Bingoogus, Moonflare and Deskel mentioned a good chunk of it, besides others maybe, i skipped like 10 pages.

First of all, update was good.
I wish that what we learned, will now be the grounding point for the lore.
Wouldn't even mind if Sel went out from there and retconned things in the past and adjusts future things from here on, hopefully removing story/general junk.

1.
While reading .53 something came up again that i read from Sel and or a character way back.
"What do you think happens to characers in a game after you finished it/ after you shut down your PC?",
"Will they continue living their daily lifes?"

It's very philosophical and i see it in connection to "Can a wish make a wish?", or i don't know,
Can your dreams live on or something.

Which might be what Maya symbolizes, as a wish that made a wish.
Which leads me to 2.

2.
This one is very, as people say, tinfoily, and i wouldn't hold it against one.
I once went down the rabbit hole of trying to see if character names might have a meaning in japanese.
But to cut it short, that was rather fruitless, Makin' Ami, and the sorts.
Came to the conclusion that it was rather pointless, not that some names had some interesting meanings, like Himawari.

But, here comes the butt.
When i read .53, the second thing that came up with all that Himawari was willing to share, was the term "Deus Ex Machina".
I don't think i get 100% what the term means but it's like "Something happening that seems like a wonder, even without a god doing it."
I really have a hard time explaining what i mean here.

And if i take all that together, with what Maya is and that i think she's related to the Wire God, i wonder if Maya is supposed to symbolize the concept of a "Deus Ex Machina".
And if (here is the boiled down tinfoilery) her last name does hold some meaning, maybe it is the Machina/ Makina part (don't know about the mi part though.)

What i do know is, that in japanese Makina is a used term. ( Kakushite! Makina-san!! )

As Bingoogus said, afair, Ami keeps her memories because she killed/kills herself.
And while i would like to go with that, don't even remember anymore if something like that was explained in .53,
there is something that might conflict with that.

And that is how at least once live (for us to see), Ami faked her death.
Which was right before another reset (Karaoke event before Maya Prime pop/ Times New Roman).
With very very likely Himawari's help.

So i do wonder if Ami escapes memory wipes not by killing herself before resets, but by planting a decoy in her stead, even with Himawari's help.

With what we saw who got wiped out, Futaba, Rin, espacially at least part of the Tsukioka? family,
i wonder if Bingoogus was right about the "keep memories", holds true for them.
There are at least two threads still left with the scarf and Tsubasa, that Himawari was involved with.

Finally:
With all the Ami, Scarf, Tsubasa and what not threads still left, espacially with Hima-chan very very likely helping aunt Ami, as was already said, even behind the "that's confidential", there's still some room left to fully trust Himawari.

posts.content_html_raw:
So, as promised, I managed to catch up with the updates and with the thread, I ran out of reactions a few pages ago so I'm sorry for not being able to appreciate all of the great posts so far.

And let me just say one thing: What a time to come back from a hiatus!
Those last two updates were amazing. In fact, since I had to go from 0.51 to 0.53 and didn't visit this thread at all and didn't know what was coming, I was under the impression for the longest time that Ayane's epilogue was just gonna be a small additional storyline after the reset is initiated by Himawari (i.e. the ending bit of the reset update 0.52) but then it went on and on and on, and it was so painfully wholesome and perfect, that instead of just playing for a few more minutes I had to stay up all night and play through it all, because damn, I didn't realize just how much I needed Akira to collect a big fat W like that. And Ayane too, of course.

One of the 0.53 haters in this thread mentioned something to the effect that he disliked the epilogue because to him Ayane was a mid-character anyway.
This is where I want to strictly disagree, as someone who didn't rate Ayane very highly myself, this whole development really catapulted her up the ranks, for obvious reasons. Seeing her this happy and fulfilled should feel satisfying to anyone who likes this game, regardless of whether you found her very interesting or not so far.

But anyway, I just want to summarize this update with one image:
A decent beach event. Not too much filler and some pretty straightforward "fan service", is what I would probably call the lewd events. And while I would usually be opposed to that (e.g. with the fan fest that really didn't speak to me much), those scenes were pretty intense and enjoyable. Or as Akira said:

I know there are a lot of Kirin haters and Noriko is a notoriously unlucky and underappreciated character in the game itself, but that scene, whew!

The Futaba crash out felt significant, but I couldn't quite make sense of it, as in why now, why her? And I didn't see anyone coming up with a good explanation yet either, other than that she had a similar, yet less random and more justified, reaction back when she read Nodoka's book. Did the "truth" just kind of come to her in her sleep-depriced state? She calmly talked with Akira just prior to the beach event, so it must have been something sudden or spontaneous. Was it godly intervention? Himawari played down the impact of gods on people and compared it to invasive ads to their brain, but I'd argue that it can still very much sway people and make them change the world on the god's behalf. Was the duplicate Futuba a hint towards that? Who knows.
My best bet is that it's one of those crash outs that characters occasionally suffer from just when they are at the brink of a crisis. Like Otoha when she was about to break up with Rin, Ami several times when she wasn't getting her way or Nodoka when she was getting too deep into the sauce (of the upside down house lore). It might however be the first sign of the dark routes manifesting, where the girls spiral down into a state of realizing how toxic their relationship with Akira actually is and how it does not resolve their trauma but threatens to worsen it for them. Yikes.

As a lot of people already mentioned here, the Maya death scene felt weirdly cheap. Like something Sel thought up like years ago as an hommage to Se7en, just with the impact lessened considerably. And I wouldn't even say so because it hit NuMaya and people dislike her. I'm sure it would have felt as inconsequential if it were, say, Tsuneyo's or Yasu's head. It would be shocking, sure, but more so in the gross and "wtf Ami, really?!" way than actually making the player upset about it. Because we already know that the reset was coming and that they will be back anyway. I didn't quite get that particular scene, other than it being the catalyst for the reset I guess. Seeing that Sel apparently wanted to evoke more of a reaction from it, even though it proved at the end of 0.53 to not have any real consequence anyway, feels more like a hurt ego of a wannabe David Fincher, rather than a clever plot point. Oh well, you can't always hit bullseye.
At the very least, the reset puzzle was somewhat bearable this time, still nothing really interesting and definitely not engaging, but there have been far worse ones in the past.
Selebus, you madman, you did it again. When the haters started to doubt you (me included), you went ahead and COOKED.
Like him or not, he is a good writer and he finally proved it again in this update. Like many others already phrased it more eloquently than I could, he knew what the story needed. He released the anchor on board a directionless ship and made sure everyone knew where they stood.
So many questions answered, such significant lore drops that we can still feast on them for months. And the promise that Akira does have a redemption arc, that he can and will change, for he now has an embodied goal to strive towards, a sense to live. And thank the ever-living fuck that it's not Ami anymore!
This whole epilogue was so god damn wholesome and pure, it actually felt like fixing me too, for having hope for Akira and believing in him. Fuck yes.
That being said, I apparently count towards the few smooth brained individuals who didn't immediately see the inevitable conclusion of it coming and basically yelled at my screen when Himawari did the very reasonable thing of erasing those memories from them.
As I said, it makes sense. It would interfere with their decisions going forward and in a time-travel/bootstrap paradox context, it's fair to say that they should come to any conclusions on their own as much as possible.
It still hurt to watch them have their memories of their daughter erased like that, that's messed up man. I get that it's probably also somewhat fan-servicey to show us those memories, but yeah. Cruel.

Also, just to piss off Bingoogus I actually really liked the music choices in this update and as opposed to the Good Kid songs, they didn't feel distracting. Especially that finale of course with the "All that's left are the stars" setting the mood, chef's kiss. Like I said above, Absolute Cinema. Selly delivered.
So what is there left to say?
Here's a few more tidbits that I have been thinking about:
Not trying to stroke his dick ego too much, but kudos to Sel for two things:
1. He essentially drafted the first purity route and left it for us to do the consumer testing. I mean, what else are those wished dimensions other than what has to have been Sel's plan for the purity routes. Himawari being the engineer, it's all set in motion already. It's actually a really clever way to implement those in a way that makes total sense within the story.
2. Christoween? Christmalloween? I already forgot what he called it. It's dumb, yes. But it's actually clever, considering he is a lazy piece of shit (sometimes). Instead of having to do two special updates revolving around unique costumes etc. that are also supposed to be close to each other within the calendar year and ideally also somewhat align with the release date, he only has to focus on one now and can release it anywhere between October and January with it still fitting the real life setting. And he even made it actually kind of make sense within the storyline of things getting more and more jumbled up in this world.
Proud member of the Ami haters club. I really don't see how anyone can still seriously cheer for her or have any hope of short-term redemption for her character, when she outright said she is willing to kill anyone (including Akira, aka her Dad, himself) just to get her way and stay in this world.
Unless she is the uber mastermind and is tricking everyone after all, she has basically been degraded to a villain of comical degree. Especially now that Akira realizes how it actually feels to have a real daughter, it must be clear that there is no future for Ami becoming anything else but his enemy in his new goal of getting back to Himawari.

She is now also confirmed to have divine protection, which explains a few things, though not everything. Who's that god? I'm not convinced yet that it has to be Sekai, even though it would make the most sense right now.

I also like that people suggest there is a copy/clone of her that she (Prime Ami) sacrifices to the custodians to ensure her memories and powers stay in tact. That would make sense.
I just don't get how that screenshot of those 4 Amis next to Himawari fits in all that. If those are all copies of Prime Ami and that's the real Himawari, it would mean she would be aware and that the custodians would know of her tricks. Unless, somehow, Ami has the same power and is able to create copies of anyone, including Himawari? That would feel a bit cheap and would potentially change the meaning of past scenes where it was suspected that they didn't involve the real characters but where it also wouldn't make sense for it to be Himawari. I don't know.
I might actually have a tinfoil theory regarding the above, involving Ami, Maya, Himawari etc. but it's not really based on too much substantial evidence or anything, so maybe I'll post about it later.

Happy to be back and be able to read and contribute to the thread again.

I mean, what else are those wished dimensions other than what has to have been Sel's plan for the purity routes. Himawari being the engineer, it's all set in motion already. It's actually a really clever way to implement those in a way that makes total sense within the story.
2. Christoween? Christmalloween? I already forgot what he called it. It's dumb, yes. But it's actually clever, considering he is a lazy piece of shit (sometimes). Instead of having to do two special updates revolving around unique costumes etc. that are also supposed to be close to each other within the calendar year and ideally also somewhat align with the release date, he only has to focus on one now and can release it anywhere between October and January with it still fitting the real life setting. And he even made it actually kind of make sense within the storyline of things getting more and more jumbled up in this world.

spoilers.title: Ami
spoilers.html:
Proud member of the Ami haters club. I really don't see how anyone can still seriously cheer for her or have any hope of short-term redemption for her character, when she outright said she is willing to kill anyone (including Akira, aka her Dad, himself) just to get her way and stay in this world.
Unless she is the uber mastermind and is tricking everyone after all, she has basically been degraded to a villain of comical degree. Especially now that Akira realizes how it actually feels to have a real daughter, it must be clear that there is no future for Ami becoming anything else but his enemy in his new goal of getting back to Himawari.

She is now also confirmed to have divine protection, which explains a few things, though not everything. Who's that god? I'm not convinced yet that it has to be Sekai, even though it would make the most sense right now.

I also like that people suggest there is a copy/clone of her that she (Prime Ami) sacrifices to the custodians to ensure her memories and powers stay in tact. That would make sense.
I just don't get how that screenshot of those 4 Amis next to Himawari fits in all that. If those are all copies of Prime Ami and that's the real Himawari, it would mean she would be aware and that the custodians would know of her tricks. Unless, somehow, Ami has the same power and is able to create copies of anyone, including Himawari? That would feel a bit cheap and would potentially change the meaning of past scenes where it was suspected that they didn't involve the real characters but where it also wouldn't make sense for it to be Himawari. I don't know.

posts.content_html_raw:
You know, something I think doesn't get talked about enough...is how fucking amazing the soundtrack for this game is.

Everyone has their own little soundtrack, songs that you associate with just them. Some songs are specific to the tone of a scene(Looking at you Hallelujah.mp3).

New songs pop up at just the right moment in the story to frame a scene in such a way that it just magically hits.

I'll be the first to admit that I often play games muted and listen to my own music, so when I started this game with the warning that it shouldn't be played that way, that the sounds and music were an important part of the game...I was a smidge skeptical.

I learned pretty quickly that I was wrong. The soundtrack for this game is phenomenal.

spoilers.html:
Proud member of the Ami haters club. I really don't see how anyone can still seriously cheer for her or have any hope of short-term redemption for her character, when she outright said she is willing to kill anyone (including Akira, aka her Dad, himself) just to get her way and stay in this world.
Unless she is the uber mastermind and is tricking everyone after all, she has basically been degraded to a villain of comical degree. Especially now that Akira realizes how it actually feels to have a real daughter, it must be clear that there is no future for Ami becoming anything else but his enemy in his new goal of getting back to Himawari.

She is now also confirmed to have divine protection, which explains a few things, though not everything. Who's that god? I'm not convinced yet that it has to be Sekai, even though it would make the most sense right now.

I also like that people suggest there is a copy/clone of her that she (Prime Ami) sacrifices to the custodians to ensure her memories and powers stay in tact. That would make sense.
I just don't get how that screenshot of those 4 Amis next to Himawari fits in all that. If those are all copies of Prime Ami and that's the real Himawari, it would mean she would be aware and that the custodians would know of her tricks. Unless, somehow, Ami has the same power and is able to create copies of anyone, including Himawari? That would feel a bit cheap and would potentially change the meaning of past scenes where it was suspected that they didn't involve the real characters but where it also wouldn't make sense for it to be Himawari. I don't know.

Moonflare said:
Now, we know that wishes go to another version of you that didn't wish for them. That would mean that Kaori from another reality made some sort of wish that granted this Kaori Nao-chan.
Click to expand...
I'm not sure this is true. It's ambiguous, but I think when someone wishes for a person (rather than a world), that person is created in the world in which the wish was made.

Himawari draws a clear distinction between wishes that create worlds and wishes that create people.
Most people wish for their own perfect world. The world the wish is made in already has its own fixed existence (which is probably someone else's wish), so their wish world has to be created elsewhere and they never even know their wish came true, much less get to see it.

I predicted that part long before this update (humble brag), but the part that confused me was that I assumed wishing for a person is just a more specific version of wishing for a world (e.g. when Akira wishes for Maya, he's actually wishing for a "perfect world" where Maya exists). I still think that would make the most sense mechanically, but it doesn't appear to be the case. Wishes that create a person don't also create a corresponding world.


From this it's an open question of whether the new person is created in the same world or in a preexisting world elsewhere, but of those two options the former makes a lot more sense to me. There's no reason for Person A's wish to create a new person in Person B's world.
From what we know about Kaori's wish for Nao-chan, it makes more sense that our Kaori made that wish rather than one in a different world.
If a Kaori somewhere else wished for Nao, this world's Kaori shouldn't know about it, but she does:

(Side note: the way Kaori phrases that makes me think someone (Sensei?) is going to break the "one wish" rule the same way Maya broke the "wishes can't make wishes" rule.)

In fact, we might have even seen Kaori making her wish:

Why I think she's wishing to be a mothermom here:
  • She's looking up at the stars, which she says make wishes come true.
  • The purple sky matches the purple color of Nao's aura. This is according to Kaori and also seen in a bunch of renders with Nao.
  • This happens right after Kaori chases the white cat, a symbol of USER4. USER4 is tied to Nao-chan as the holder of the TEMPLATE9 backup (possibly they were the one who chose how to fulfill the wish), and also Nao's eyes = Ami + Maya = USER4
Of course this has interesting implications for Akira's wish that created Maya. That would mean the Akira in Maya's original world was the one who wished for her, and if my understanding is correct:
  • Akira wished for Maya in the same timeline in which he later met her. His wish didn't retroactively change the past.
  • Akira's wish didn't change anything about his world other than plopping Maya down into it.
One consequence of the second point is that if Maya was created from something, that something didn't already exist in Akira's world. So a brilliant theory such as "Maya used to be a part of Ami" doesn't work because it would require Akira's wish to change the Ami that already existed in his world.

The first point is even more interesting for me, since I still believe Maya was around before the accident, which would mean he didn't wish for her as a replacement for the dead Sekai. The things we've inferred about Maya's fake backstory (homeless, molested by a relative) make it seem like Akira wished for someone he could save. Himawari did imply this is the case, though it's unclear if she knows the full specifics of his wish.

We don't know what kind of love she's talking about here. I have no evidence for it, but I quite like the idea that Akira's wish was supposed to be wholesome, that he wanted to save someone the same way Sekai saved him, but without the accompanying sexual relationship. That's what Akira wanted when he was a child, he never understood why his savior also had to be his tormentor.

First off, this is a very complex topic and anything related to alternative worlds/universes and branching timelines ends up being a mess and basically boil down to one core question:
Can there even be an OG timeline/reality?
If a world is created from a world, that was created from a world, etc. and all its inhabitants placed in it being essentially clones of the previous world (I guess?) does it make them not real anymore? What makes someone real in such a universe, in which there might have been an infinite amount of worlds prior to this one that contained different versions of characters? How would you even rationalize distinguishing between a person that has been wished into existence by someone and a version of a person that is the creation of a world that is only someone's wish? It's just all so heavily philosophical.

I know this is drifting towards a different direction now than what you were addressing, but to come back to it, personally I'm also on Moonflare's side. To me, Hima-chan's explanation hints rather towards both worlds and people being created outside of the world from which the wish originates.
I think this very quote you provided is actually more supportive to Moonflare's case, Himawari does not distinguish between a world or person when referring to a wish, indicating that a wish is always something that only comes to fruition in a different world.
I agree with you about Kaori though, it does seem like "our" Kaori made that wish and that it manifested within the same world. However, we don't know that for a fact, it may have been indicated but not shown. We don't know enough about Kaori's backstory, what she really was like prior to the accident or even in a past timeline. Maybe the Kaori that wished for Nao-chan (i.e. becoming a mother, or maybe something more directly related to Ami and Maya?) was one that actually died in the car crash.

At the end of the day, since anyone could have wished for anything (once, at least), it's difficult to say what is supposed to be real, fake, a wish or whatever else you would call it.

The origin of Maya is an interesting question as well.
To me, it was always implied that Akira couldn't live with the trauma of losing Sekai (combined with the more subconscious trauma she caused him directly) and most likely wished Maya into existence (probably not literally, but as in "I wish there would be something or someone to ease my pain" or something to that effect) in a timeline where he ultimately ended his life.
So that in another world, where everything happened more or less the same, Maya appeared and as a consequence of fulfilling the wish (depending on how it was phrased/intended) ended up falling in love with Akira.

Now since we know that Maya wished for this world (Terminal 23), it means that something still went wrong in the world she originates from. I suppose one of the major questions to this storyline is finding out what happened to make her wish for this world so bad, that she defied divine laws that have never been broken before. Was it simply the fact that she wasn't able to save Akira? Was it the fact that he ended up hating himself for what he has become, the guilt of being a predator?

What's probably essential here is to look at what this world in which the story takes place (Terminal 23) actually represents. What could have Maya wished for that created it?
Given that it's main characteristics are that it resets much quicker than other worlds, that it is stuck both in a loop and physically through the wall where nobody can leave Kumon-Mi and that virtually any female character that gets in contact with Akira is feeling drawn to him to an unnatural and illogical degree, it must have to do with Maya wishing for Akira to never leave and to learn to accept his condition (as opposed to getting rid of it). I could see such a wish causing to create a world that is forcing Akira to stay and never leave, while also making everyone accept his way of living since he never faces real consequences and everyone is weirdly okay with his predatory behavior (which he himself even questions all the time).
Himawari even mentions Niki once as an example, implying that it just seems surreal and illogical that his childhood sweetheart turned out so obsessed with him that she became a famous pop idol as a result, who still loves him the most. She is maybe the most obvious embodiment of this world's skewed worldview where everything seems to orbit around Akira, everyone loves him, despite his many flaws and mistakes.
Which now also brings me to another point that I was hinting at in my previous summary post.
Opening up this pandora's box of "any world and any person could just be someone's wish", essentially only begs further questions.
It's tinfoil hat time now. We know for a fact now that Maya and Nao are examples of characters being wished into existence.
But who is to say that there haven't been others before?

What makes Maya and Nao special? They both seem to defy certain divine laws. Maya is able to manifest a wish despite being a wish herself. Nao seems deeply connected with the gods as well, frequently travelling to other dimensions.
Now, class, who else do we know of that seems to have some divine connection and hidden powers? Hmm?
Ami. I mean, think about it. We have speculated about her knowing much more than she pretends to for the longest time. That she is similar to Maya in that regard. And now, we have the confirmation that she does have divine protection. And that she is much more powerful and knowing, at least in her current form.
And, there is even several reasons why she would have been wished into existence:
1. The most obvious one would be that Sekai wished for a daughter, possibly even specifically from Akira. Maybe it was more vague, maybe she wished for a way to be able to be with Akira, and the gods found it humorous to manifest it by her becoming pregnant by him (resulting in Kyoto).
2. I could even imagine Nozomu being the one actually wishing Ami into existence. We don't know enough about him to really speculate too much about this, but whether it would be to fulfill his wish of a daughter or to help Sekai find peace in a more roundabout way?
3. Very unlikely but maybe it was even Akira. In his case, definitely not a literal wish, but maybe also a wish to rationalize his relationship with Sekai or to "fix" her. Maybe she abandoned him in another world and he wished for her to be forced to stay with him, hence a child was born (again, Kyoto).
Now obviously this would go against the rule of only having one wish, the other one being confirmed to be Maya. But maybe...Maya was not supposed to exist because of this fact alone? Maybe it's a red herring that the issue was that Maya has had a wish fulfilled despite being a wish herself, maybe Akira started it by having been granted two wishes, becoming the target for many gods? Very far fetched, I know, just wanted to throw it out there.

One specific reason why I would find it fitting if this theory turned out to be true though is that it would create an interesting end scenario for this storyline.
Given that the main story is essentially about Akira overcoming his trauma (with everyone else's in the purity routes), it could boil down to Akira having to realize to let go off his initial wishes. He would need to face the fact that he himself has it in him to save himself, to change, that he does not need divine intervention to deal with his predatory behaviours due to trauma. Meaning that Maya should cease to exist the moment he realizes that his problems are not solved by copying Sekai but by defying her and healing from the mental wounds she has inflicted to him.
And similarly, he should have never have to wish for a justification for staying with Sekai, for interpreting their relationship as love, for forcing something into it that should not exist. In other words, that Ami should have never existed.

Thus, resulting in an endgame Ami vs. Maya, where Ami would fight to do anything to stay "alive" as a wish (assuming the logic is similar to why gods exists, as Pareidolia said: "I only exist, because you believe in me.") and create her perfect world, whereas Maya wants to stay with Akira forever, both having to ultimately learn that if they exist for Akira and truly love him, they both have to cease to exist for him to grow and become the person he needs to be to become truly happy, i.e. become a loving Dad to Himawari (assuming it's the canonical ending).

Now obviously Nao-chan would have to fit in there as well, since she bears both Ami's and Maya's eye colors, which can hardly be a coincidence, but I can't really think of anything clever here right now that would connect her to this scenario directly, especially since she is mainly connected to Kaori.

Is this likely what Selebus has in mind for the endgame, since he says he knows how it will end? Probably not. But some of the context provided so far could at least justify believing in this being a possibility.
However, in case I haven't bored you to death yet, I have another curve ball to throw at you:
Himawari also was only a wish? *cue dramatic music and Moonflare yelling in the distance*
I admit, this one is even more out there as a theory and I myself would prefer if this weren't true.
But it could make sense. During the whole of 0.53 and basically throughout the whole game itself, Hima-chan just feels....too perfect? You must have felt it too, no?

I want to explain this by Sel just being really into his own characters and actually wanting her to be this perfect, almost a Mary Sue of Lessons in Love.
But...I don't know, it could also be an epic reveal that she herself has only been a wish (most likely of course Ayane's, maybe even connected with her (not confirmed) abortion? Maybe Himawari was, as gruesome as it may be, Ayane's wish for the abortion not to take place?).
Maybe it would even go so far as, like others have already started to speculate (screenshot of her and 4 Ami's), her being in the same team as Ami?
Maybe they both fear their fate of being not needed anymore by a "cured" Akira, hence working together to direct him towards a future that is supposed to ultimately stop him from changing and just wishing to stay in this world in which both Ami and Himawari can exist.

I just can't completely detach myself from this thought, it all just seems very convenient and straightforward from here. Almost like it's a trap. The world seemed perfect, but they also basically cut themselves off from all of their friends (except for Sana). Their whole belief and happiness hinges on Himawari herself. Have they both really become their best version? Like Akira said himself, he hasn't really "deserved" this ending. They both deserve to come to their conclusion by themselves, to realize that Ayane's role is to be the mother she never truly had and for Akira to grow up and take responsibility for his actions, which essentially he didn't seem to have actively done in that world. It has been forced upon him. And the moment that both of them seem to start to develop independently from Himawari ("Let's make another baby") and Ami comes into play (Akira having to face his problems from the past) Hima-chan conveniently ends this "simulation" to not have them think about such scenarios and focus on her.

But yeah, to be fair, I don't really believe in this one myself, there's a lot of subjective interpretation forced into this. And I just don't see Sel going this far off the rails and ultimately do believe Himawari to be the intended and genuine "end goal" for this story.
Okay, this was a lot.
I'm obviously not as solid of a theory crafter as the heavy hitters here, but maybe some of you guys can draw something from this or at least give me peace by disproving my thoughts, I might have forgotten about some details that could be relevant here or that would go against some of those takes.

I'm sure Terminal 22 will play a big role, including the upside down house, Nodoka and now Shiori. What's the deal with Kaori and Nao-chan, etc.
I'm confident that Sel's masterplan is complex enough for neither of us to decipher too much of the story this far in advance, even after this massive lore drop. But that's what makes it so much fun to theorize.

So that in another world, where everything happened more or less the same, Maya appeared and as a consequence of fulfilling the wish (depending on how it was phrased/intended) ended up falling in love with Akira.

Now since we know that Maya wished for this world (Terminal 23), it means that something still went wrong in the world she originates from. I suppose one of the major questions to this storyline is finding out what happened to make her wish for this world so bad, that she defied divine laws that have never been broken before. Was it simply the fact that she wasn't able to save Akira? Was it the fact that he ended up hating himself for what he has become, the guilt of being a predator?

What's probably essential here is to look at what this world in which the story takes place (Terminal 23) actually represents. What could have Maya wished for that created it?
Given that it's main characteristics are that it resets much quicker than other worlds, that it is stuck both in a loop and physically through the wall where nobody can leave Kumon-Mi and that virtually any female character that gets in contact with Akira is feeling drawn to him to an unnatural and illogical degree, it must have to do with Maya wishing for Akira to never leave and to learn to accept his condition (as opposed to getting rid of it). I could see such a wish causing to create a world that is forcing Akira to stay and never leave, while also making everyone accept his way of living since he never faces real consequences and everyone is weirdly okay with his predatory behavior (which he himself even questions all the time).
Himawari even mentions Niki once as an example, implying that it just seems surreal and illogical that his childhood sweetheart turned out so obsessed with him that she became a famous pop idol as a result, who still loves him the most. She is maybe the most obvious embodiment of this world's skewed worldview where everything seems to orbit around Akira, everyone loves him, despite his many flaws and mistakes.
