posts.content_html_raw:
My thoughts about the update:

Overall, I think it was a good update. It was a good follow-up to the best update in the game, in the sense that things have changed, and the lore drops continue. It's basically like we're in another stage for LiL, as it should be.
I think the general theme of the update went back to a breather for the most part:
lots of silly jokes and ambient conversation. In regard to the lore drops, I think we've seen a lot of them. Going from the Sekai buried under the tree, to a lot of people knowing about stuff and confirming it with eachother. All in all, it's, like I said, a new stage - and thus the need to set up where everyone's at.
On the other hand, we've also tied up loose threads of personal arcs and that's all over the place. If I had to point one of them out it's that Futaba's arc is just pathetic.
The whole thing with her parents being dead was just fixed by Shiori and the whole Nodoka publishing her entire sex life on a book was just that. A nothingburger. Futaba can't have an arc for the life of Selebus.

There are also other threads connecting, like Io and her "friends", their mutual take on sex. The situation with Yasu, the whole Yumi x Chika x Noriko thing. A considerable part of the update is about "hey, remember that thing that happened, yeah it happened!". I think that's a good and necessary thing, it just works sometimes and at times it highlights how it went nowhere.

Like Akira saying that Yumi has a problem with Nodoka, and yet there's no variation for if Nodoka actually sexually assaulted/blakmailed her. Cause that's more than "a problem".

Now, to the main arcs happening. Let's just address the Maki thing, which I thought was wildly out of place.
I get that she's worried because she now knows what Akira's been through, and if she focused on that it'd be fine. But what the fuck is up with freaking out about girls dressing up for halloween, what the hell. She's the actual owner of a sex shop that had gangbangs next door of her infant child. Thank god for Makoto pointing that out because she's even more pathetic in this update than Futaba.

I guess Selebus chose to have her be the "voice of reason" with many caveats to contrast her with Haruka (that just goes pathetic predator here - MULTIPLE TIMES). But here's my major gripe with this: there are zero variations that address Sara finding out about Sana. Don't you all think this would be relevant to all the scenes she's been present at, including talking to Sana? I think this was a letdown.

On to Haruka, I think that was a good update for her. Storywise it just highlights that there really is something around Akira that makes him desirable, I guess. Or maybe she just sucks, after all Molly did invite her to a threesome with Akira. And if the option was Haruka + Akira to any of the girls, many of them would say yes. So yeah, being a predator is bad, who knew. I like that she disses Chika though:
On to the highlights of the update:

I'm not going to comment much on either Maya or them remembering fragments of Himawari through Yasu because it was great, but I don't have much to add. I really enjoyed that Maya told him all of her memories and, if you think about it, it's just uncanny that she wouldn't be a wish. I mean, how do you justify not remembering anything before being twelve (or whatever age) and waiting in the rain?

Nodoka's stuff was interesting, but also on the trail of "confirming paranormal things". There should be a post just collecting all of these later. Like Yasu saying the lie that this world was made by Nozomu, or confirming that Sekai is indeed the world itself:
Now to the interesting and also lame conclusion of an arc: Chika.

As I said, I liked that Haruka dissed her and I liked even more that she finally touched reality from her talk with Yumi. Cause yeah, she's been really pathetic all throughout and especially during the conversation. "Hey, I rejected this girl that loved me, and now after she finally worked up the courage to go after the guy she likes, I'm going to fuck with her head because my "boyfriend" won't pay attention to me" - all the while, the girl she almost threw from a balcony, is nonchalant "yeah, and my mom is dying, you know, that one person in the family that you lost?". And Yumi is just like "Can I get my food now?".
I love Yumi in this scene because she is very kind to Chika if you think about it. Chika didn't deserve even half of this from the shit she pulled (and is pulling). Anyway, I quite enjoyed the developments up until this point, but then, when we get to the final scene, I just felt like I couldn't care less. Her arc took WAY too long and I just can't be bothered. My exact emotions watching her "confession" were "can't you just shut up and go away?" - at the end of the day, isn't she acting even MORE selfishly by dumping all of this on Rin and not even wanting to hear a reply?
Yikes, I think I'm good with Chika for a full year. Bunch of self-serving bullshit. Fuck off and go take care of your sister, dude.

Also, can we just hightlight that Futaba can't even STAND UP FOR HER FRIEND? For real, what has Futaba ever fucking done?
Mind you, I think Otoha was right. Rin got this. But why would Futaba listen to Otoha of all people? The person that hurt Rin the most out of everyone here? It's like every opportunity Selebus has to make Futaba pathetic, he goes all in.

Finally, Kirin. Get fucked. You deserved MUCH worse than what your TSS was. I'm not condoning Haruka here because it was much more about Haruka than her. Actually, even Sana and Sara's response was more interesting than Kirin there.
But I don't know, good for her that Nao-chan saved her I guess. Good things happen to horrible people.
There was a lot of lore that was dropped in the update as well, and I didn't cover most of it here. Figured I'd tackle a bit of the character stuff this time. Also, I think Selebus lost his touch a bit on some of the narration. Too much rambling - not to an extent that it became boring, but I struggled not to jump a few lines. And tbh I just give up on reading anything written in cursive.

Anyway, nice update. I think the major flaw was not including more of the Sara variables, but the fact that it highlighted that we're on a new era for the game is a huge win (along with everything Maya related).

I really enjoyed that Maya told him all of her memories and, if you think about it, it's just uncanny that she wouldn't be a wish. I mean, how do you justify not remembering anything before being twelve (or whatever age) and waiting in the rain?
Spoiler
Nodoka's stuff was interesting, but also on the trail of "confirming paranormal things". There should be a post just collecting all of these later. Like Yasu saying the lie that this world was made by Nozomu, or confirming that Sekai is indeed the world itself:
Spoiler
Now to the interesting and also lame conclusion of an arc: Chika.
As I said, I liked that Haruka dissed her and I liked even more that she finally touched reality from her talk with Yumi. Cause yeah, she's been really pathetic all throughout and especially during the conversation. "Hey, I rejected this girl that loved me, and now after she finally worked up the courage to go after the guy she likes, I'm going to fuck with her head because my "boyfriend" won't pay attention to me" - all the while, the girl she almost threw from a balcony, is nonchalant "yeah, and my mom is dying, you know, that one person in the family that you lost?". And Yumi is just like "Can I get my food now?".

My exact emotions watching her "confession" were "can't you just shut up and go away?" - at the end of the day, isn't she acting even MORE selfishly by dumping all of this on Rin and not even wanting to hear a reply?
Spoiler
Yikes, I think I'm good with Chika for a full year. Bunch of self-serving bullshit. Fuck off and go take care of your sister, dude.

was right
. Rin got this. But why would Futaba listen to Otoha of all people? The person that hurt Rin the most out of everyone here? It's like every opportunity Selebus has to make Futaba pathetic, he goes all in.

Another implication about the true nature of Ami's suffering

So I read this as likely a symbolic reference to Akira's subconscious view of his older brother/guardian, but it sparks questions of whether or not this has a deeper, more literal meaning to the overarching narrative. As in, what if the original "world" that the original Akira and others are actually from was a creation of Nozomu's wish. Unlikely and not much evidence actually points to this, but Hima did say that wishes weren't supposed to be able to make wishes, not that people that live in worlds created by wishes couldn't make their own wishes. Just a thought.

Also even more confirmation that this figure represents Nozomu, not that there was any doubt.

Iiiiiinteresting, so she was dreaming and feeling Shiori's presence. Very interested to see learn more about her mother and how they are connected. Cool that Nodoka is finally getting some progression and has finally seemingly unlocked the truth, about time.


Honestly "Nu Maya" is winning back some points for me

Post-Nut Clarity reference :O
How far we've come already

Another very impactful line that I feel could have multiple meanings... On the surface it's very heartwarming and exciting to finally learn about their past. Her being the one who came on to him makes a lot of sense and possibly hints to why she has been such an exception in so many ways. Not only was she the "first" victim of his, but she was the most pure since he technically wasn't the one who pursued her in his mind. Within his psyche, perhaps he was free from some of the guilt that he should've had with the dynamics of this kind of relationship, which fits as to why he feels so attached to her.

posts.content_html_raw:
Well that was a ride...

- Firstly, the elephant in the room.

...Wow.

Haruka has got to be the most insufferable fucking character in the game at this point. Like, what redeeming qualities even are there? Her and her actions do make for a nice comparison to Akira (why are we fine with it when he does it VS when she does?), but in all honesty, Haruka comes off as just... really sad, desperate and pathetic in this update.

Say what you will about Akira, but while he's shown us those same qualities on numerous occasions, at least he wasn't a full blown rapist about it. At least, not of his own volition outside of a blackout/divine intervention. Haruka doesn't even have any tragic backstory excuse to fall back on either. She lived a comfortable, normal life in her early years.

She just... fucking sucks.

I really hope she gets what's coming to her and that Sara catching her actually goes somewhere. Not to mention Chika knows about it and so does Kirin obviously. I dunno what she was thinking was gonna happen. That's such a huge gamble she made... twice. Like... do you even care about your reputation at this point?

Oh! And then there's Sana! As if she couldn't sink any lower, she lets Haruka drag Kirin away, despite Kirin begging for help and she even misleads Noriko to go and search in the wrong direction when she's concerned about her friend. Like?????

Damn, man... I guess Sel really wants to hammer home the point he made that 'Sana has never been a good person'. I can see that clear as day now.

And yeah, I know that some may see it as karma for what Kirin did to Ayane way back when, but... in my opinion, that's a pretty shortsighted take to have. Sexual assault isn't okay. It wasn't okay when Kirin did it to Ayane, when Nodoka did it to Yumi, when Ami did it to Maya, or even here. I'll never see that as a fitting punishment in this situation, especially when Ayane already personally handled business herself back in Chapter 3.

So yeah... in essence, Haruka and Sana are both on my shit list now. I hope to see the aftermath of all this sometime soon.

- On a brighter note, it's nice to see Maya finally got her first proper h-scene! It was a pretty good one too. Not the best I've seen, but it was really fitting and they had a good conversation about Maya's past. It's nice to see that finally confirmed for both us and Akira. Ami actually kept her word and stayed away too! Hell yeah.

- Yasu was as cute as ever! I really feel for her, wanting to make friends so bad, but has to struggle with constantly hurting others or scaring them off. She really deserves all the best... and maybe a proper hug too (Shame on you, Akira! You hug the Yasu and don't just stand there!).

- Oh yeah! And now we more or less have confirmation that Nozomu is HOPE! Well... it's been kinda half confirmed since Chapter 1, but, now we heard it straight from Yasu's mouth.

- On a more depressing note once again, it will never get any easier watching Chika's life fall apart. Now she's burning bridges with people who genuinely care and want to help her. She confesses to Rin finally, but then... straight up cuts her off immediately afterwards.

Like... what??

I just know Rin's gonna start spiraling again, just as Futaba feared. So yeah... unfortunately it didn't pan out the way you thought, Otoha.

Of course, I could always still be wrong, but guess we'll see.

- Did Makoto ever talk to Yumi like Akira instructed her to? I don't think they talked even one time this update lol. So much for being on top of things, Makoto.

- Maki was not messing around in that conversation with her friends. Nice to see she's actually being responsible and is perhaps more understanding and cautious after her talk with Akira (when the two Sekai's showed up). She has to be aware that Sensei and Makoto have hooked up, yeah? Like... she has more than enough pieces to have already solved that puzzle.

Especially when she says things like:


- Ayane is definitely aware of some things again, but seeing as the only thing we got was some text at the very end that didn't amount to much, we won't get to know exactly what she remembered until next time.

- Nodoka's events were interesting as always. Especially that talk of becoming a god yourself. Also, I guess she's an unofficial member of the RAS now?? Maybe? Things should get even more interesting when she shares what all she knows.

- What haven't I touched on yet... Oh yeah, Tsubasa says Sekai isn't buried under the tree in their garden...

...Calling BS on that one personally.

- Ami was as Ami as always. Kinda a dick move to mess around with Uta's feelings like that when she's already struggling so hard lol. She's trying to keep Akira as blissfully ignorant as she can, but... the truth will have to come out sooner or later.

Overall, I'd say this was an 8/10 update. Pretty good. I had fun at least. It wasn't nearly as good as the previous update, but honestly, I'm okay with that. After a two-part Reset and a huge lore dump, it was nice to take a bit of a breather. We got some important tidbits such as confirmation on Maya's past and how they met, as well as some setup that will no doubt prove vital in updates to come in the near future.

I'll be looking forward to it.

spoilers.title: 0.54 Thoughts
spoilers.html:
- Firstly, the elephant in the room.

...Wow.

Haruka has got to be the most insufferable fucking character in the game at this point. Like, what redeeming qualities even are there? Her and her actions do make for a nice comparison to Akira (why are we fine with it when he does it VS when she does?), but in all honesty, Haruka comes off as just... really sad, desperate and pathetic in this update.

Say what you will about Akira, but while he's shown us those same qualities on numerous occasions, at least he wasn't a full blown rapist about it. At least, not of his own volition outside of a blackout/divine intervention. Haruka doesn't even have any tragic backstory excuse to fall back on either. She lived a comfortable, normal life in her early years.

She just... fucking sucks.

I really hope she gets what's coming to her and that Sara catching her actually goes somewhere. Not to mention Chika knows about it and so does Kirin obviously. I dunno what she was thinking was gonna happen. That's such a huge gamble she made... twice. Like... do you even care about your reputation at this point?

Oh! And then there's Sana! As if she couldn't sink any lower, she lets Haruka drag Kirin away, despite Kirin begging for help and she even misleads Noriko to go and search in the wrong direction when she's concerned about her friend. Like?????

Damn, man... I guess Sel really wants to hammer home the point he made that 'Sana has never been a good person'. I can see that clear as day now.

And yeah, I know that some may see it as karma for what Kirin did to Ayane way back when, but... in my opinion, that's a pretty shortsighted take to have. Sexual assault isn't okay. It wasn't okay when Kirin did it to Ayane, when Nodoka did it to Yumi, when Ami did it to Maya, or even here. I'll never see that as a fitting punishment in this situation, especially when Ayane already personally handled business herself back in Chapter 3.

So yeah... in essence, Haruka and Sana are both on my shit list now. I hope to see the aftermath of all this sometime soon.

- On a brighter note, it's nice to see Maya finally got her first proper h-scene! It was a pretty good one too. Not the best I've seen, but it was really fitting and they had a good conversation about Maya's past. It's nice to see that finally confirmed for both us and Akira. Ami actually kept her word and stayed away too! Hell yeah.

- Yasu was as cute as ever! I really feel for her, wanting to make friends so bad, but has to struggle with constantly hurting others or scaring them off. She really deserves all the best... and maybe a proper hug too (Shame on you, Akira! You hug the Yasu and don't just stand there!).

- Oh yeah! And now we more or less have confirmation that Nozomu is HOPE! Well... it's been kinda half confirmed since Chapter 1, but, now we heard it straight from Yasu's mouth.

- On a more depressing note once again, it will never get any easier watching Chika's life fall apart. Now she's burning bridges with people who genuinely care and want to help her. She confesses to Rin finally, but then... straight up cuts her off immediately afterwards.

Like... what??

I just know Rin's gonna start spiraling again, just as Futaba feared. So yeah... unfortunately it didn't pan out the way you thought, Otoha.

Of course, I could always still be wrong, but guess we'll see.

- Did Makoto ever talk to Yumi like Akira instructed her to? I don't think they talked even one time this update lol. So much for being on top of things, Makoto.

- Maki was not messing around in that conversation with her friends. Nice to see she's actually being responsible and is perhaps more understanding and cautious after her talk with Akira (when the two Sekai's showed up). She has to be aware that Sensei and Makoto have hooked up, yeah? Like... she has more than enough pieces to have already solved that puzzle.

Especially when she says things like:


- Ayane is definitely aware of some things again, but seeing as the only thing we got was some text at the very end that didn't amount to much, we won't get to know exactly what she remembered until next time.

- Nodoka's events were interesting as always. Especially that talk of becoming a god yourself. Also, I guess she's an unofficial member of the RAS now?? Maybe? Things should get even more interesting when she shares what all she knows.

- What haven't I touched on yet... Oh yeah, Tsubasa says Sekai isn't buried under the tree in their garden...

...Calling BS on that one personally.

- Ami was as Ami as always. Kinda a dick move to mess around with Uta's feelings like that when she's already struggling so hard lol. She's trying to keep Akira as blissfully ignorant as she can, but... the truth will have to come out sooner or later.

Overall, I'd say this was an 8/10 update. Pretty good. I had fun at least. It wasn't nearly as good as the previous update, but honestly, I'm okay with that. After a two-part Reset and a huge lore dump, it was nice to take a bit of a breather. We got some important tidbits such as confirmation on Maya's past and how they met, as well as some setup that will no doubt prove vital in updates to come in the near future.

I'll be looking forward to it.

posts.content_html_raw:
Nodoka: I just realized how to get over my own instinctual dislike for Nodoka: pretend she has a surgical mask on that has her signature dumb smug smile drawn onto it - then just look at her eyes instead. At some point Nodoka mentioned that she often has trouble making her outer presentation and her inner emotional state match, which means even though she always looks smug and knowing, she's not always feeling smug and knowing (even though she does feel that a lot).

It makes me miss all the times she's not trying to be smug and knowing because I think she's being insincere. Ignoring her mouth and just looking at her eyes at least allows me to process what she's saying without getting distracted by how much I want to..I dunno, punch her or something.

Chika: Why have I related so so much, so consistently to aspects of Chika's stories? First to the tension Sensei felt knowing that Chika was head over heels for him in a way he wasn't for her (pre rabid breakdown) and now to the very specific sensation of feeling so lost in the pursuit of romantic happiness that you feel like you lose pieces of yourself in the process.

The reactions - the emotions written - they struck so close to home, in such specific ways that I can't imagine Sel hasn't experienced this himself before. I've literally looked back on my life and friendships after falling down a romantic goddamn well and felt horrified and responsible for how trashed they were because I was too lost in said well.

Maya: It's clearer than ever after her post-coital heart-to-heart that she is a wish-construct. To appear, memory-less, before Sensei at what was clearly a "rock bottom" moment for him - crying and wandering around the Old District in the rain - it was that state he was in where he made that wish.

Given how Maya implies that Akira didn't start coming back to her smelling like strawberries until some time had passed (enough for her to get attached first so that she can subsequently start getting jealous because of the change), my personal belief right now is that Akira must have made his wish shortly after the car accident that took Sekai and Nozomu.

Haruka: So fucked. It's an actually incredible depiction of someone trying something for the first time, lent confidence by spending a lot of time watching and admiring an expert but not actually taking the time to learn what MADE that person an expert, and fucking it up as a result. Dunning-Kruger at work. Except applied to something deeply fucked up. Haruka said, a few times, things like "I don't want to make you uncomfortable" and "I don't want to take advantage of you" and I fully believe that she doesn't want to do those things, yet she put zero mind and effort to actually doing anything that would meet those intentions.

I'm sure if she was in her right mind aka not brokenly insecure from a night of feeling rejected by her friends and by Akira that she might have been more mindful of those things. But hell, no amount of good intentions can overwrite that she set out to go prey on a teenager to satisfy her lust and loneliness... and I'd rather not get in the habit of making any sort of excuses for that sort of behavior.

But this situation is definitely going to get a lot worse before it gets any better.

Kirin: all of the TSS scenes have been beautifully done surreal illustrations of the involved characters, but I think this one might have been my favorite. It communicated Kirin's interiority so perfectly.

Ami: waiting for just about anything redeeming here. Nothing yet. In the meantime my hackles are raised every time she's on screen, now. Maybe she'd get a minor kick out of that. But maybe not. People who've gone sociopathic are kind of unpredictable like that.

Generally: kind of nice how many of the plot points that have been hinted at are being reinforced openly, now. Feeling lost in a haze of surreal implications was getting a little trying. The "I acknowledge Christmas" thing is also a nice, effective way to get a clear count of who's avoiding the mental clear-outs from the timeloops. Aside from the Rooftop Apocalypse Squad, there's Ami, Tsubasa and Nodoka. No confirmation on Tsuneyo this time.

spoilers.text:
Nodoka:
I just realized how to get over my own instinctual dislike for Nodoka: pretend she has a surgical mask on that has her signature dumb smug smile drawn onto it - then just look at her eyes instead. At some point Nodoka mentioned that she often has trouble making her outer presentation and her inner emotional state match, which means even though she always looks smug and knowing, she's not always feeling smug and knowing (even though she does feel that a lot).
It makes me miss all the times she's not trying to be smug and knowing because I think she's being insincere. Ignoring her mouth and just looking at her eyes at least allows me to process what she's saying without getting distracted by how much I want to..I dunno, punch her or something.
Chika:
Why have I related so so much, so consistently to aspects of Chika's stories? First to the tension Sensei felt knowing that Chika was head over heels for him in a way he wasn't for her (pre rabid breakdown) and now to the very specific sensation of feeling so lost in the pursuit of romantic happiness that you feel like you lose pieces of yourself in the process.
The reactions - the emotions written - they struck so close to home, in such specific ways that I can't imagine Sel hasn't experienced this himself before. I've literally looked back on my life and friendships after falling down a romantic goddamn well and felt horrified and responsible for how trashed they were because I was too lost in said well.
Maya:
It's clearer than ever after her post-coital heart-to-heart that she is a wish-construct. To appear, memory-less, before Sensei at what was clearly a "rock bottom" moment for him - crying and wandering around the Old District in the rain - it was that state he was in where he made that wish.
Given how Maya implies that Akira didn't start coming back to her smelling like strawberries until some time had passed (enough for her to get attached first so that she can subsequently start getting jealous because of the change), my personal belief right now is that Akira must have made his wish shortly after the car accident that took Sekai and Nozomu.
Haruka:
So fucked. It's an actually incredible depiction of someone trying something for the first time, lent confidence by spending a lot of time watching and admiring an expert but not actually taking the time to learn what MADE that person an expert, and fucking it up as a result. Dunning-Kruger at work. Except applied to something deeply fucked up. Haruka said, a few times, things like "I don't want to make you uncomfortable" and "I don't want to take advantage of you" and I fully believe that she doesn't want to do those things, yet she put zero mind and effort to actually doing anything that would meet those intentions.
I'm sure if she was in her right mind aka not brokenly insecure from a night of feeling rejected by her friends and by Akira that she might have been more mindful of those things.  But hell, no amount of good intentions can overwrite that she set out to go prey on a teenager to satisfy her lust and loneliness... and I'd rather not get in the habit of making any sort of excuses for that sort of behavior.
But this situation is definitely going to get a lot worse before it gets any better.
Kirin:
all of the TSS scenes have been beautifully done surreal illustrations of the involved characters, but I think this one might have been my favorite. It communicated Kirin's interiority so perfectly.
Ami:
waiting for just about anything redeeming here. Nothing yet. In the meantime my hackles are raised every time she's on screen, now. Maybe she'd get a minor kick out of that. But maybe not. People who've gone sociopathic are kind of unpredictable like that.
Generally:
kind of nice how many of the plot points that have been hinted at are being reinforced openly, now. Feeling lost in a haze of surreal implications was getting a little trying. The "I acknowledge Christmas" thing is also a nice, effective way to get a clear count of who's avoiding the mental clear-outs from the timeloops. Their first memories (first contact), presumably, involve them both meeting their wishers in the rain, and being taken in by them:
(Chapter 4 Maya 'Something To Do With Love' Event)

(Chapter 3 'First Contact' Main Event)

This also suggests multiple things such as:
  • Nao-chan is possibly the same age Maya was. (Maya should have been around 7, since it was 8 years ago when Sekai died, and Akira ghosted Niki, with his relationship with Maya beginning within months afterwards.)
  • Akira may have knew Maya was his wish and was sent to find her, like how Kaori was sent to find Nao-chan.
  • Wishes that are people, seem to end up in the world of their wisher. Kaori is well aware that Nao-chan is her wish.
  • This also suggests that Maya knew she was a wish like how Nao-chan does.
  • They also both may have inherent supernatural powers. Maya probably just doesn't remember after all of her Resets. (which may be by design. Wanting to be a Normal Teenage Girl.) Nao-chan may have actually been trying to get Maya to realize what she could do recently.
  • The Rain is likely significant.
Haruka should have went after Uta or Molly, but no, she went after a crying girl in a bathroom, and little red riding hood, to really lay on how Haruka was the big boobed bad wolf this update. (Seemed reminiscent of Sensei's early days with Io, Miku, and Yumi. And more recently Karin.) Watch it be as impactful as Haruka getting caught fucking at her business was.

I also appreciate how Kirin, who I consider probably the most mundane/"normal" of the girls, had a rather "normal" predator sexually harassing her, in Haruka. This event couldn't really happen with any of the other extra eccentric characters, because they wouldn't have reacted just like a confused and conflicted teenage girl in such a vulnerable situation, would. Like if it was Makoto, Nodoka, Sana, or Uta, etc, this would have gone way different.

This is why Kirin is necessary in my opinion. She's as close as it gets to an average teen girl in this game, and her events seem to be grounded compared to others. Even her TSS was realistic. Just replace the stage with social media, and the audience with any followers that actually like her, after she posted herself doing slutty shit online for likes.

(Chapter 4 Niki 'That Funny Feeling' Event)
(Chapter 4 Haruka 'Blood In the Water' Event)
I still think Sana is going to be Ami's antithesis, though.

Ami ultimately caring, even when she's callously hurt, while Sana ultimately doesn't, even while callously hurting others.

(Chapter 4 'Silver & Gold' Main Event)
Sana seems to be the girl that uses Sensei the most for what he is instead of who he is, while pretending to care about him, because it works.

posts.content_html_raw:
Overall I really liked the update. We got a ton of character lore and drama. Lotta thoughts/tin foil cause fuck work, I wanna talk about everyone's favorite wholesome game instead.

Akira staying proactive is a massive relief, with even Makoto acknowledging it. Enough of the relationship balls are in the air to where we can have some real progression while the drama naturally unfolds. All the setup, I think, is done. Now we'll begin to see everything crumble down into the dark route. I believe the next several updates will include ticking time bombs in the relationships blowing up spectacularly.

Kirin - Having her be red riding hood is on the nose but suitable. We're seeing actual growth from her, she's acknowledging that her chasing sex was just a distraction from her wanting emotional connection. She even now wants to hold hands! She deserves a lot of hate for her SA of Ayane and her prior callous attitude, but she did not deserve Haruka (Trash). Even with Akira, it never felt so gross and crass. I think this will kick off a desire to apologize again to Ayane, as Kirin now felt firsthand how awful it was. I only hope that Ayane has recovered from Yasu's unintentional Himawari attack to as to not reject it violently. However, I'm afraid that's exactly what will happen causing Kirin to sink further.

Her TSS was on point thematically, but I think could have gone harder TBH. Loved to see Nao rescue her though.

Nodoka - Good to see her becoming more human, even setting up Maya. Good girl Nodoka! I think her interactions with Sekai tells us something. She actually felt Sekai. This isn't just a haunting from Akira, but Sekai has an actual presence. Tsubasa was 100% lying, Sekai is buried beneath the tree, and might be the "base" for the world. Perhaps that's why she can actually physically interact.

Futaba - Unfortunately boring end to parents/going crazy arc. Boo. However, she rightfully tried to stop Chika. She has good instincts, but stupid Otoha stopped her. Bad Otoha.

Maki - We see Maki being the only rational adult with Trash (Haruka) and Sara. She rightfully stands her ground and directly draws the line in the sand. Trash is already too far gone, and Sara is held emotionally captive by Sana (who might actually be truly evil.) If/when everything becomes "public", Maki will be leading the charge. The only thing that might mitigate it is her sympathy for Akira. She's clearly acknowledged in her head explicitly what their driving conversation was, and Akira's nature. Her remarks on the attire were protective both towards Akira and the girls. She thinks she can still stop it, but its too far gone.

Makoto and Maki - This I see as the biggest time bomb relationship wise with a ENORMOUS elephant in the room. Maki's audible escapades were perhaps not the best thing for a young impressionable Makoto. So while Maki is 100% correct in her fear for Makoto and the rest of the girls, it will fall on deaf Makoto's ears. The inevitable confrontation may irreparably harm their relationship when the full truth comes out. Its gonna be real bad, and will domino effect every other relationship.

Sara - Poor Sara. She wants nothing more then to love her family and provide a good life for Sana. But Sana, who might definitely be pure evil, has her held captive in emotional chains. Sara is in an impossible position, especially after Maki's declaration. She's now caught Trash (Haruka) red handed too. I can only hope she acts the part of the woodsman and kills the evil trash wolf.

Sana - What happened to our shy girl. Was she always just a sociopath? Was what happened in that one beach event we couldn't see what corrupted her? She knowingly let Kirin be taken away to be raped. She knew, she saw, she went "Heh". Talk about a wolf in sheep's clothing. I really hope its just the gods fucking around, but I'm afraid this might be the real Sana.

Maya - Loved everything about it. From her standing up to the incest goblin, to her talk with Akira. We finally get some concrete points of how they met. It felt very similar to how Nao was found by Kaori and Akira, likely relevant later on. I think her initiating really fits strongly with the idea of her being Akira's wish. He very clearly hates that part of himself, so of course he'd want a way to "mitigate" the blame he puts on himself. We even have Maya outright saying it was a Lesson in Love. NuMaya rocks, and is now forging her own special bond with Akira through honesty. While NuMaya and Prime Maya are both the "same person", Prime Maya never told Akira these things. She might have been rightfully scared it would break him, but now NuMaya has something Prime Maya never did. An equal playing field between her and Akira. Cannot wait for more Maya events. Co-Best Girl status with Ayane regained and affirmed.

Yasu - Loved to see her rounding out. She's found a good balance between normal girl and religious vessel. Her reply to Miku was hilarious. Her unrequited hug was sad, and she didn't mean to make them pseudo remember Himawari. Her naming Nozomu God I think confirms he is Hope. If we put together that along with Sekai being buried beneath the tree, this suggests Hope is INTIMATELY related to the nature of the world. He was the first godGOD we met which lends further credence. Maybe his hope is to revive Sekai? Continue to torture Akira? IDK but there's definitely more there.

Tsubasa - 100% definitely lying about Sekai's body. She instinctively remembered Christmas, so further confirmation she's Meta aware/immune to the nature of the world. Why is she lying? It must relate back to her saying its out of love for her family and wanting to save them. We can't quite see the shape of her plan, but its deeply related to Sekai. Whose body is absolutely under that tree, buried beneath their feet.

Ami - Still an incest goblin whose seeming practical rationality is matched only by her unhinged willingness to do anything to get what she wants. I love that Akira is being confrontational with her, and cannot wait to see it develop further. For all her crazy unforgiveable shit, I think Akira might be able to get through to her. We saw her briefly unnerved by Akira throwing her mistakes in her face. Perhaps that will be her Lesson in Love.

Chika - Chika you ignorant slut. The first several scenes gave me such hope. I loved her violent sadness, and thought her realizations of herself would truly hit home. I even think that they might have, if not for the big bad TRASH wolf being in the wrong place at the wrong time.

Her confession to Rin was nothing less then emotional rape and cowardice. From the nature of it and how she went about it. She knew Rin had finally accepted her feelings for Akira and was in a truly happy place. (Which to be fair Chika was still struggling with Akira being a Himbo but I digress.)

Its one thing to lay all that out, but to not even let Rin respond?!? "See you at school"?!? Pure selfishness. She didn't care how it would effect Rin, she just cared that Rin wasn't hers. She only did it to vent and make herself feel better.

That's not to say there isn't some context. I think her violent sadness was corrupted by both Akira's past actions and TRASH wolf's overture. I think the depth of Chika's feelings for Rin and how she let them out was a distorted corruption of her real feelings. Call me crazy but the possessiveness and depth for Rin specifically seemed to grow 100 fold in this update alone. She liked her, but this was on a whole nother level. This tells me that she was sad that Akira wasn't only hers, and violently angry/disgusted at Trash Wolf. This caused an emotional nuclear reaction in the poor girl, who we can now clearly see was never good at dealing with them.

Still, Rin is too good a homie to do that too. Bad girl Chika.


Trash Wolf - You unmitigated piece of garbage. You deserve Io's "Unburnable Trash" sweater line tattooed all over your body. You are so far off the deep end you've drowned in your own trashiness. You actually made Akira look good by comparison, which is an insane thing to say. For all the shit he's done, the only true "non-con" was when his body was taken over.

This felt like Io's mom. This was raw sordid sleaze. It felt more uncomfortable then Stomachache. At least that has some emotional catharsis and context attached that came later. This had no emotion other then selfish hunger. Trash Wolf was just that, a true predator chasing her Red Riding Hood.

IDK how anyone who learns of can respond with anything other then revulsion. The coming confrontation will be ugly and tragic.

There's going to be a lot of emotional fallout in the coming updates.

spoilers.title: Chika
spoilers.html:
Chika - Chika you ignorant slut. The first several scenes gave me such hope. I loved her violent sadness, and thought her realizations of herself would truly hit home. I even think that they might have, if not for the big bad TRASH wolf being in the wrong place at the wrong time.

Her confession to Rin was nothing less then emotional rape and cowardice. From the nature of it and how she went about it. She knew Rin had finally accepted her feelings for Akira and was in a truly happy place. (Which to be fair Chika was still struggling with Akira being a Himbo but I digress.)

Its one thing to lay all that out, but to not even let Rin respond?!? "See you at school"?!? Pure selfishness. She didn't care how it would effect Rin, she just cared that Rin wasn't hers. She only did it to vent and make herself feel better.

That's not to say there isn't some context. I think her violent sadness was corrupted by both Akira's past actions and TRASH wolf's overture. I think the depth of Chika's feelings for Rin and how she let them out was a distorted corruption of her real feelings. Call me crazy but the possessiveness and depth for Rin specifically seemed to grow 100 fold in this update alone. She liked her, but this was on a whole nother level. This tells me that she was sad that Akira wasn't only hers, and violently angry/disgusted at Trash Wolf. This caused an emotional nuclear reaction in the poor girl, who we can now clearly see was never good at dealing with them.

Still, Rin is too good a homie to do that too. Bad girl Chika.

Ami's situation is more fantastical so I can see her being redeemed story-wise and turning a new leaf at some point but I can't see myself being able to view her positively again, personally, but I can see how someone else might depending on how things go.
Click to expand...
I have been thinking quite a bit about the Ami situation from every event she's in, under the light that Selebus claims she's the character we know the least about - and, even though, I assume there will be huge plot-twists meant to make us sympathize with her, I just... can't see it.
Let's say the reveal is that this isn't the actual Ami, but then we'd be sympathizing with another character instead.

Or let's say she has a reason for doing all of these things, maybe providing entertainment for the gods, or remaining a "question they can't solve", and thus a reason for them not to shutdown the TERMINAL 23. In that way she'd be "doing the work no one else would want nor could do in her stead". But I'd still find it hard to justify liking her in that situation, given the glee she has with raping Maya.

Let's say she's just a very broken girl, be it from her situation, having lived for thousands of years, or being assaulted by gods/hellbent on doing whatever she can so that she doesn't lose herself to them as well. I mean, it's a repeat of my feelings - sure, maybe I can understand it, but that's not exactly liking her.

I fear the more time goes on with Ami being a hateful character, the more Selebus risks being unable to have enough time to reverse course. On a logical level, sure. Who knows what the justification will be, since it's likely fantastical. It's just that, if I'm reading a story and the final justification of a villain is that they're brainwashed, while I do logically understand I can't blame them, I have also spent the entire story hating them - and there's just not enough time left to spend learning to love the character vs time spent hating them. It also can just easily fall into the first example of "this is just a different character altogether".

Regardless, Ami has been (to me) a creepy character that I sympathize with for her situation, then just a creepy character, then someone that I was rooting for on her daughter arc, to becoming an even creepier and hateful character. Where in this is the part where I like her?

One possibility I might enjoy is that there's just no redemption for Ami, she's an actual villain and the bittersweet ending is giving her a purity route where she just never had to go through all of it - and thus never became a villain.
At the end of 10 years of releases, I just hope the math actually maths and that it wasn't 80% of "Ami was a bizarre foil" and 20% of "she's actually good but there's not enough time to emotionally get invested in this vs all the road so far".

posts.content_html_raw:
Seriously, I've forgotten just about everything that's happened so far, including even this update, so I'd appreciate any and all reminders that invalidate my takes



First, Kirin. I like what this update did for her. To me, Kirin's whole thing is her control over how others want her. She never had control over what her parents thought of her. She grew to resent Ayane because she denied her the clearest shot she had at being able to command her family's respect. She's proud of herself in that her sex appeal wraps Akira around her finger. She's convinced herself that she's a nympho because it puts her in control of how others perceive her. And here, Haruka gives Kirin a wakeup call that she doesn't actually care about control or being wanted. She wants to be seen, and Haruka shows her what it's like to be sexualized without being seen. And she's disgusted by it.



Strangely enough, Kirin's TSS pushes her right back into that box just as she gets this strong impetus to climb out of it. All of the TSSs so far have just had me throw up my hands, but this is the first one that makes me wonder if they're meant to keep the characters trapped in their emotional infancy. If anyone has any insight into what the TSSs are and how they ought to be interpreted, I'm all ears.



Point is, I love Kirin. For the same reason I love Akira. For the same reason Haruka is very much a ??????? to me. Childhood trauma can be REALLY messy. It worms its way into your head and pops up in ways that may seem to have no rhyme or reason to them. It contorts and compartmentalizes your brain, sometimes so extremely that you become multiple people. This story reminds me that there's beauty even in being broken, that compassion is triumphant.



On that note, Haruka. What the fuck? She just likes to leer at kids just 'cause. She just thinks it's hot. Someone find her a therapist before she hurts herself or anyone else. Correct me if I'm wrong, but besides his blackout with Yumi and Karin (Karen?) it's all been Akira leaning into his fucked up sense of intimacy. It feels like Haruka is meant to be a foil for Akira, and also a reflection of players (that's you!) who play this game just to get their rocks off. I feel like this will be explored more with the wizard content that's apparently coming up.



Maki. I forgot what she talked about with Akira when they went camping. Evidently they talked a bit about Sekai, and some folks here have suggested she might suspect Makoto's sleeping with him. Personally, I think there's a distinction to be drawn between her sex positivity (and age-appropriate communication of that with Makoto) and her neglect of Makoto. She deserves to be proud of the fact that she didn't teach Makoto to be puritanical about sex, but she seems to be proud of the fact that she's kinda been a useless parent otherwise. I think it's fair for Makoto to be skeptical about Maki when she's failed to prove herself to be reliable in this way. However, I don't think that makes her concerns any less valid. Knowing what she knows about Akira (which apparently I do not), she has good reason to believe the kids are at risk of turning out like Kirin. I think it's good that there are some decent parents in the game. It's interesting narratively, plus it grounds the game in a sense of morality that feels way more real. This isn't a depraved universe, there are just depraved (mostly traumatized) individuals.



Chika. She's so hard on herself. She was going to school, working, caring for her immunocompromised little sister, all without parents around. And now that the Tsukioka family is giving her all this stability, she has way more freedom to consider her needs and her wants and what being even a little bit selfish means to her. Naturally, she's going to want dependable stability and commitment from a partner, and naturally she's going to be attracted to that in the most forthright, dependable person she knows. Rin. Especially with Akira turning her world around and whatever supernatural entity spun her around with it. She was rude to Yumi, sure, but I admire how vicious she is when it comes to protecting her peace. I also don't remember exactly how her conflict with Yumi went, so take that how you will. Generally, I don't think she really did anything wrong. Love you queen. Hope Rin chases you down and steps up for you. I don't see why she wouldn't.



With that, I really just have a bunch of stupid person questions for a stupid person.



So Sana seems to me to just be a super masochistic nympho. And she seems to enjoy others' suffering vicariously. Less sadistically and more like using their experience to fuel her fantasies (kinda like reading a visual novel hmm). My question is when did this shift happen? It kinda came out of left field for me. She hasn't always been like this, has she? Also, what does she think about Sara?



I might've mentioned this before, but what exactly are these Transpacific Sadness Symposia? Whose perspective are they describing? Are they real? Or just symbolic? What is their purpose?



Literally what is going on with Ami and Sekai? Like, from the top. I see either of them and I get sooooo confused my eyes just glaze over. I'm like yep okay she knows something. Shrug. Apparently she's been repeatedly raping Maya? Huh? Seriously I know nothing.



Finally, a bit of a smaller question, but why did Chika start working at the maid cafe again?

Nozomu being a god is a direct reflex of him "being a god" during the time Akira was abused by him - as said in game. Sekai, along with her name, was, in fact, his entire world. It would be wild that Sekai only exists in this world thanks to Maya though But, furthermore, maybe everyone that exists here is a direct reflection of Akira's perception of things? If we asked ourselves "how would a mother behave, if she knew her daughter's former teacher and close friend/sex partner was a traumatized pedophile?" - I don't think we'd get to "she'd start telling every girl she meets to dress up less slutty for halloween".

It's not that there's fault in this writing, it's just that... well, they weren't in the first place. It just comes across as bizarre and off target, and I think that's where people are coming from (I am at least). I think the point was that Maki's so out of it that she'd make a huge deal out of nothing, because it was never about the costumes, but about what she isn't able to rationalize.

So, on one hand, Makoto is right in pointing out that she's behaving like a lunatic. Because she is. If she was complaining about the girls putting on a swimsuit contest and having Akira judge it, sure. Or the million of other examples that there have been. There's just none in this update.

Makoto was clearly traumatized by Maki/her father having groups of people gangbanging her mom every saturday, and I can surely see someone like that just ignoring any attempt of said woman trying to dictate what she can or cannot do sexually, even though Maki'd be correct in doing so.

Moonflare said:
Nozomu was actually named as a god way back. But, yes, I agree that this is more evidence, especially along with "the world itself being Sekai", and the flash between Nozomu, the god, and Nozomu the brother.
I have been thinking that maybe they're both right? This world is Maya's wish, but what she wished for is very much unclear. It could even be that "HOPE" and "The World Itself" are Maya's creations.
View attachment 5491075
Nozomu being a god is a direct reflex of him "being a god" during the time Akira was abused by him - as said in game. Sekai, along with her name, was, in fact, his entire world. First because she got him out of the closet, his one ticket to the world outside of the abuse. And then that he was bereft of a world after "his world" died.

Also, do mind that HOPE, Wires and Pareidolia are called "makeshift" gods (though I can't recall exactly when and by whom). But it would make sense if they're a by-product of Maya's wish. In fact, Pareidolia being fished out of the well for reasons he himself doesn't know how, would also fit into this - because it wouldn't have been by Akira, but by Maya's wish.

My point here is that the original Nozomu and Sekai were maybe just people, but it's Akira's perception of them that made them a god and the world itself. And that Maya's wish was to create a world for Akira, that ended up reflecting his own mental perception of things.

It would be wild that Sekai only exists in this world thanks to Maya though But, furthermore, maybe everyone that exists here is a direct reflection of Akira's perception of things? That they're real, but they're the version of themselves that adhere to his tastes (that both work for and against him?)

I agree, and I'd like to expand on that, since I have seen some comments talking about not understanding why people didn't like Maki's stance in the update.
I think what annoys me about Maki is that she's going about this in the wrong way. If we asked ourselves "how would a mother behave, if she knew her daughter's former teacher and close friend/sex partner was a traumatized pedophile?" - I don't think we'd get to "she'd start telling every girl she meets to dress up less slutty for halloween".

It's not that there's fault in this writing, it's just that... well, they weren't in the first place. It just comes across as bizarre and off target, and I think that's where people are coming from (I am at least). I think the point was that Maki's so out of it that she'd make a huge deal out of nothing, because it was never about the costumes, but about what she isn't able to rationalize.

So, on one hand, Makoto is right in pointing out that she's behaving like a lunatic. Because she is. If she was complaining about the girls putting on a swimsuit contest and having Akira judge it, sure. Or the million of other examples that there have been. There's just none in this update.

On the other hand, as Makoto points out, Maki has zero leg to stand on. She's totally morally bankrupt here. Her argument as a mother is sound "I don't want my daughter, nor anyone's daughters to be taken advantage of by an adult" or even "I don't want a good friend to have to deal with more temptation when he's clearly traumatized and unable to function". Either is fine. It's just that, would a daughter of Maki listen to Maki?

I think that's the point Makoto's making here. It's not about her being right or not, but that she created a relationship where she just wouldn't be taken seriously by her daughter, that being Makoto or not. It's kind of like how Sara feels about trying to tell her daughter not to have sex with her teacher (what she should be doing btw).

Makoto was clearly traumatized by Maki/her father having groups of people gangbanging her mom every saturday, and I can surely see someone like that just ignoring any attempt of said woman trying to dictate what she can or cannot do sexually, even though Maki'd be correct in doing so.

Alas, she's going about it in the wrong way and Makoto's aware of the resets, so it's like... what Maki thinks really would make zero difference for her. And that's not even counting "bluejay", since dying kind of tops the issue of "mom wants to say who I can't have sex with".
Edit: Someone that remembers, please help with the "you're a son of makeshift gods" thing. I can't recall from where it is.
Click to expand...
That makes sense to me as well. You're def onto something with the world being a reflection of Akira's perception. I can't grasp what the exact wording of the wish might have been, but the effects seems clear with that tick tock evidence.

Maya's wish created a world that accentuated Akira's deepest desires and perceptions. Therefore, Sekai is literally the world, with her poetry themes influencing everyone in it to some degree. Nozomu is a distorted HOPE, an overbearing evil entity. Everything and everyone seem to move to Akira's apparent benefit, allowing him to live out a "dream world" of endlessly indulging in his darkest desires. This Frankenstein world attracts the other gods attention, and ropes in the other beings of the well.

spoilers.title: Maki
spoilers.html:
I think what annoys me about Maki is that she's going about this in the wrong way. If we asked ourselves "how would a mother behave, if she knew her daughter's former teacher and close friend/sex partner was a traumatized pedophile?" - I don't think we'd get to "she'd start telling every girl she meets to dress up less slutty for halloween".

It's not that there's fault in this writing, it's just that... well, they weren't in the first place. It just comes across as bizarre and off target, and I think that's where people are coming from (I am at least). I think the point was that Maki's so out of it that she'd make a huge deal out of nothing, because it was never about the costumes, but about what she isn't able to rationalize.

So, on one hand, Makoto is right in pointing out that she's behaving like a lunatic. Because she is. If she was complaining about the girls putting on a swimsuit contest and having Akira judge it, sure. Or the million of other examples that there have been. There's just none in this update.

On the other hand, as Makoto points out, Maki has zero leg to stand on. She's totally morally bankrupt here. Her argument as a mother is sound "I don't want my daughter, nor anyone's daughters to be taken advantage of by an adult" or even "I don't want a good friend to have to deal with more temptation when he's clearly traumatized and unable to function". Either is fine. It's just that, would a daughter of Maki listen to Maki?

I think that's the point Makoto's making here. It's not about her being right or not, but that she created a relationship where she just wouldn't be taken seriously by her daughter, that being Makoto or not. It's kind of like how Sara feels about trying to tell her daughter not to have sex with her teacher (what she should be doing btw).

Makoto was clearly traumatized by Maki/her father having groups of people gangbanging her mom every saturday, and I can surely see someone like that just ignoring any attempt of said woman trying to dictate what she can or cannot do sexually, even though Maki'd be correct in doing so.

Alas, she's going about it in the wrong way and Makoto's aware of the resets, so it's like... what Maki thinks really would make zero difference for her. And that's not even counting "bluejay", since dying kind of tops the issue of "mom wants to say who I can't have sex with".

While I agree that someone like Chika, Kirin, to some extent Futaba and most notably Haruka have been portrayed as pathetic characters (though personally I would rather call them "flawed" instead, with the exception of Haruka, more on that later), I find that that's not a sign of bad writing but, on the contrary, a smart and interesting choice for character development.

As per the above example, I agree that Futaba should know better in theory, but in practice it makes sense that she would not understand Rin in this situation. As Otoha says, Futaba lacks the gaydar, while being the much better friend than Otoha would ever be, some aspects Futbaba will never understand as well as someone like Otoha.
Is it somewhat frustrating that she cannot grasp Rin's emotions and can't wrap her mind around certain things? Sure. But is it believable that she doesn't, given that she has a lot of shit on her mind in the first place and is generally a way too sensitive and naive person for her own good? Absolutely.
She is a flawed character, and I like it about her. And I feel it is necessary for LiL characters to not be Mary Sues, but to have bad character traits and behave erratically and illogically at times.

Think of it this way:
If, for example, Chika were to reasonably and maturely resolve all her conflicting feelings and communicate it calmy with all parties involved to find the ideal solution (if it even exists), would that truly benefit the story? Would it feel authentic and believable if an emotional, possessive and traumatized parent-less 16 year-old teenager were to handle such difficult situations better than the average adult?

At the end of the day, tying up loose ends and de-escalating conflicts at this point of the story (more or less in the middle, let's call it Act 3 in context of classical plays) would be counterproductive for the development and flow of the story. We know the dark routes are still upon us, there is still need for escalation. So in my eyes, it makes total sense that these characters are flawed, that they make wrong decisions, that they misjudge and misunderstand each other still, that they keep creating conflicts and chaos.
The purity routes is where I expect the story to offer solutions, to bring closure and make characters find the silver lining and fill their holes to ultimately redeem themselves and come to a happy end.

So as much as it frustrates me too to see Chika being still flawed and unreasonable and selfish, to me it makes sense narratively and I find it portrayed very well and authentically by Selebus.

For those it just make sense, such as in Haruka's case, she wouldn't begin being a (awful) predator without her backstory with Akira influencing her, so the resulting scenes could not exist in any other path.

And trust me, I feel almost as disgusted as Kirin for this level of fanboying that I'm displaying in this whole post, but Selebus did a suspiciously amazing job at portraying the "typical" predator.

Some have mentioned that it made them realize the double standard of cheering for Akira, the predator, while booing Haruka for being essentially the same thing.
But as others pointed out, there are some very important nuances that make the way the two live out their predatorial urges differ significantly and make one much more insufferable and enraging than the other.

It has been established throughout the story already many times that Akira, while factually being a predator, not much more more but still nothing less, his reasoning and way of dealing with his urges has been portrayed as much more humane and varied than what would be the average image of what most people think of as a "typical" predator. Akira feels like having to conquer the girls. He wants them to really love him, to create this connection with him. A groomer, but a very diligent one. Prime Maya is a good example, he essentially goons over her since she is the so unavailable to him, but he respects her for it too, he actually tries his best to understand her and just ends up falling for her in the end. Now disregarding that this might be mostly due to suppressed memories and also the fact she is most likely a creation of his sick mind in the first place, and that it is inferred that similar powers might have influenced the others in similar ways, it still makes him objectively seem less of a bad guy, somehow.

Now in total contrast, Haruka is portrayed as straight up vile and primitive in her approach of dealing with her urges.
Whereas Akira is somewhat patient and cautious, often actively trying to fight his urges when being confronted with willing victims, Haruka is acting like a rabid dog, scouring for any victim to consume immediately to still her thirst. There is seemingly no rhyme nor reason to her modus operandi, she is almost comically naive about how she thinks this would work. "Sensei does this, so it can't be that hard, right?", is such a dumb, unreflective and irresponsible justification of giving in to her inner demon that it borderline hurts.

And the way Sel describes Haruka in her awkward attempt to convince a visibly terrified and unwilling victim to just give in and let the rape happen is so incredibly convincing that it makes me wonder if Sel really is that good or actually just fucked up. Luckily for him he has had the better part of 2-3 millions words of writing to convince me to tend to the former.

What I found surprising is that nobody drew the comparison to Sekai yet, unless someone did and I missed it, in which case fuck you I have ADHD sorry!
This is basically what I imagine Sekai to have been like when she first dipped her toes into the waters that is child abuse. It has been shown already how she started to convince Akira in similar ways, though much less clumsily than Haruka. But do we really know that she hasn't had previous victims?
I'm not an expert on the topic, but I would imagine that this kind of sick affinity just doesn't get triggered randomly when spotting a hot little boy (I just shuddered simply writing this expression, ew) but that it is something that has been boiling inside a person for some time before they decide to take action for the first time. And while I vaguely recall her claiming that she only ever did such a thing to her beloved Akira, I in no way trust that ghost to be a reliable narrator and not lie to his and our face to sate her disgusting desires.
Anyway, I feel like I drained my cognitive energy completely by thinking about this whole event for this long, so all I have left is a couple funny comments shitposts that I wanted to make:

Ami especially is like, 99% unredeemable (irredeemable?) for me at this point.

spoilers.title: Is Selebus a bad writer for making characters be pathetic?
spoilers.html:
Admittedly, Moonflare didn't say it outright, but the general critique was that Sel is doing everything to make certain characters look pathetic, the above quote is mostly symbolical for what I'm trying to convey.

While I agree that someone like Chika, Kirin, to some extent Futaba and most notably Haruka have been portrayed as pathetic characters (though personally I would rather call them "flawed" instead, with the exception of Haruka, more on that later), I find that that's not a sign of bad writing but, on the contrary, a smart and interesting choice for character development.

As per the above example, I agree that Futaba should know better in theory, but in practice it makes sense that she would not understand Rin in this situation. As Otoha says, Futaba lacks the gaydar, while being the much better friend than Otoha would ever be, some aspects Futbaba will never understand as well as someone like Otoha.
Is it somewhat frustrating that she cannot grasp Rin's emotions and can't wrap her mind around certain things? Sure. But is it believable that she doesn't, given that she has a lot of shit on her mind in the first place and is generally a way too sensitive and naive person for her own good? Absolutely.
She is a flawed character, and I like it about her. And I feel it is necessary for LiL characters to not be Mary Sues, but to have bad character traits and behave erratically and illogically at times.

Think of it this way:
If, for example, Chika were to reasonably and maturely resolve all her conflicting feelings and communicate it calmy with all parties involved to find the ideal solution (if it even exists), would that truly benefit the story? Would it feel authentic and believable if an emotional, possessive and traumatized parent-less 16 year-old teenager were to handle such difficult situations better than the average adult?

At the end of the day, tying up loose ends and de-escalating conflicts at this point of the story (more or less in the middle, let's call it Act 3 in context of classical plays) would be counterproductive for the development and flow of the story. We know the dark routes are still upon us, there is still need for escalation. So in my eyes, it makes total sense that these characters are flawed, that they make wrong decisions, that they misjudge and misunderstand each other still, that they keep creating conflicts and chaos.
The purity routes is where I expect the story to offer solutions, to bring closure and make characters find the silver lining and fill their holes to ultimately redeem themselves and come to a happy end.

So as much as it frustrates me too to see Chika being still flawed and unreasonable and selfish, to me it makes sense narratively and I find it portrayed very well and authentically by Selebus.

any
victim to consume
immediately

that good
or actually just
fucked up
. Luckily for him he has had the better part of 2-3 millions words of writing to convince me to tend to the former.

fuck you I have ADHD
sorry!

really
know that she hasn't had previous victims?

hot little boy

Kirin situation. Red path Kirin. Haruka situation. Flawed Characters.
Click to expand...
You quoted me so many times that I feel compelled to reply jokes aside, I feel happy that my ramblings have been useful.
I think I have said enough on the subject, but still, somehow, I still have to say this: I have never nor will ever say that Kirin deserved to be preyed upon as revenge for Ayane's blackmail. What I said (including prior to the update) was that I wished her TSS was hard/harder on her. Ironically, if on the red path, Kirin's situation here makes much less sense (as is the usual, but hold on to that point).

Also not your case, but people seem to associate having no sympathy for a sexual offender with feeling that they should be raped for justice. To the extent that some doofus was accusing me of "blaming the victim" wtf. Having sympathy for someone that is suffering a violence is just standard behavior, having no sympathy for a criminal is also standard behavior. I fail to see the issue either way.

Let's say a criminal sexually assaults your sister, and then you hear that they have been sexually assaulted - is that so hard to understand why you might be desensitized to their wellbeing that you just don't care what happens to them? Anyway, this is not directed to you, but it was something that needed to be said in order to address the rest of the post.
I feel like it might be useful to highlight that there isn't ONE red path Kirin, but at least 9 worldlines of Kirins (not even considering her Karin permutations). I'll skip the "I think I actually love Akira" from last christmas, cause everyone should remember it, it's present in all timelines and I have a lot to cover.

So, to start with the permutations: Kirin can blackmail/sexually assault Ayane, which is the big one. Then, if Miku wins the Halloween contest, Kirin will also prey on her by having her compete against her in giving Akira a blowjob while she's drugged. Then, as a minor one, Kirin will change depending on if you "kill" her during "marry, fuck, kill".

Assuming one goes complete red path here, we have a Kirin that offered to have a sexual relationship with Akira from the start, lost her virginity at a love hotel and had a threesome with Noriko - and that's it.

The green path Kirin has gone from offering a sexual relationship to Akira, to sexually assaulting/blackmailing Ayane, to losing her virginity at a love hotel, to preying on a drugged Miku, to going on a date with Akira to the sound of Ayane's song (despacito) after blackmailing her, to having the threesome with Noriko.

The green path Kirin has every reason to have her TSS. She is human garbage, she is a whore, she is a rapist, and all the things the people in the audience called her.

But what about red path Kirin? Sure, she offered to have sex with a teacher... and? If you went full red path she never blackmailed Ayane, thus she was not a rapist. She also never preyed on drugged Miku. How is this girl a monster exactly? She literally only had sex with one man, who she loves - and her roomate. So she danced to Ayane's song, but also so what? This Kirin never did anything bad to Ayane, in fact, dancing to her song is an appropriate revenge for losing the science fair. Is it because she fantasizes having sex with her sister? Or that she fantasizes with multiple women? I fail to see anything that merits this TSS.

So, in my humble opinion, once again, the red path barely makes sense. Also also, if you don't have sex with Haruka, there's just no TSS. So, in the full red path, Kirin is a girl that felt an inferiority complex towards her sister, sought sex with a teacher and then had a threesome with her roomate and said teacher. End of story. That's the entirety of her arc.
There is some dialogue, or rather narration, from this update which I think is pivotal in addressing what you talked about.

Haruka just had a regular upbringing, no real issues nor traumas, a happy marriage, until one day, because she felt very lonely for her husband being at war for years, she sought consolation at the arms of a man - and from there she started self-deprecating more and more into a bottomless hole.

If you don't have sex with Haruka, her entire arc stops at being selfish because "she felt so happy her husband was alive that she forgot to inquire about Maki's". That's it. I mean, sure, I get Maki being pissed - but let's be real, that's not the end of the world either. Cause she did feel like shit, and pursued Maki to apologise, including getting hit for it. And this, I remind you, is a Haruka that has zero self-deprecating issues. The Haruka that feels like shit because she misses her husband (and well, who wouldn't).

Why am I saying all of this though? Well, it's because the story Selebus is telling on the green path is one where Haruka never recovered from having cheated on her husband. That's the start of it all. To my eyes, it doesn't really matter to her if it's having sex with teenagers, or having sex in public, or becoming a sex slave, or just cheating - she lost herself regardless and is freefalling ever since.

I really like Haruka's story, and have since long ago. It's a pathetic character that merely lost herself entirely. If you all would remember, Haruka was missing because she almost lost her shop due to being witnessed having sex with Akira over the balcony. That's the character that on her next appearance tried to have sex with not one, but two teenagers and had to beg them both not to rat her out - all the while having other teenagers that WOULD have sex with her (Molly even having invited her previously)

If you look at the whole thing from up close it's a tragic story, but if you look at it from afar it's a comedy (which is also the blend that Selebus chooses when having her crashout on Akira, upon finding out that her husband is alive). Anyway, I do enjoy the story being told here and look forward to the next fall.
I mostly agree with you. I think flawed characters are essential to a story, and I'm talking real flaws, not the sort of "my flaw is that I care too much about people" and protagonist shit like that. One of my favorite characters in LiL is Sara.

She is a deeply flawed character, but also captivating in what she tries to be despite her flaws. Her whole interaction with Ami during their trip, or even before, when they first meet at Akira's place is amazing. And yet, her flaws make sense. Because, if she tries so hard to be a good mother, because her parents sucked, and she was broken, then abandoned, then grieving - that's the exact same reason as to why she fails at being a "proper" mother.

She'd give the world to Sana, but she also can't stop drinking, or depending on her for being unable to move on from Shota's death. She doesn't want Sana to end up like her, so she finds herself unable to restrain her enough, and would even beg Akira to keep an eye on her. I don't think anyone would say Sara's arc is pathetic by any means. She has pathetic moments, and they're great, because they make so much sense with her history that it's inevitable.

Now, let's talk about Futaba. Her entire arc in this game is a history of aborted ideas. First there was the overweight thing, which resulted in nothing other than serving as plot for Yumi - remember the gym? yeah, nothingburger (again, other than stuff for Yumi, including Nodoka meeting Yuki there).

Then there was the eating disorder arc, which led to finding common ground with Imani (who also thinks of herself as a monster). And that led to... Futaba seeing herself as a monster in her TSS... Right. What about her eating disorder though? Nope, gone to the same place as the gym.

In the middle of all of this there was the Nodoka book arc, which Futaba grew really pissed about! Because she's. the. only. one. that. cares! She cares enough to be super pissed at Nodoka and stop talking to her! Until... Nodoka says she's not going to change at all and Futaba... accepts it because Nodoka says she likes her... Hmm... it gets worse.

There was also the "I have to protect Rin" arc. In which Futaba gets super pissed at Otoha! Because she should never have been allowed to treat Rin that way, and Futaba will protect Rin so that it never happens again. Until the same Otoha tells Futaba not to protect Rin and Futaba goes "well, I guess I gotta trust you, hope you're right"

And to finish it all off: "Futaba's parents" arc. Remember when she was angry at Akira for barging in her conversation with her mom? And that she was the perfect victim because she had no parents in the country, and she felt uglier than her classmates, and she shared an interest in literature with him? And then she confirmed all of what I just said because that's how she was portrayed in Nodoka's book more or less? Well, it gets worse for Futaba because amidst this all, she still has no parents around her! and then she stops hearing from them (oh no!). Do you know where this leads? You got it! Big Nothing Burger!

And if you count, you'll realise that three nothingburgers occur in the very same update, almost in the exact same conversation

I can't see this as being good writing. Regarding Chika, I think it's much simpler to talk about. It is plausible that she'd behave exactly as she did. No issues with the writing there, in fact it's working as intended because most people got really pissed at her, and I'm pretty sure that was the intended reaction.

Now, regarding my reaction personally, I'm just tired of her. Those years of her ignoring everything in her face really soured her character to me, and while the rabies Chika is technically a new arc, it is also a continuation of acting insane. Which she has been for years. I couldn't care less about the confession or the dumping that she did on Rin, I just wanted it to be over. Rin deserves way more - and instead she first gets Rika cockblocking her, and now Chika messing with her head. At least, she does not look at Chika the same way. So the harm could have been worse.
Wow, I wrote a lot. If not everything, I recommend reading either the "red path kirin" or the "flawed characters" part, because they offer a retrospective of both Kirin and Futaba.
