spoilers.title: Red Path Kirin
spoilers.html:
I feel like it might be useful to highlight that there isn't ONE red path Kirin, but at least 9 worldlines of Kirins (not even considering her Karin permutations). I'll skip the "I think I actually love Akira" from last christmas, cause everyone should remember it, it's present in all timelines and I have a lot to cover.

So, to start with the permutations: Kirin can blackmail/sexually assault Ayane, which is the big one. Then, if Miku wins the Halloween contest, Kirin will also prey on her by having her compete against her in giving Akira a blowjob while she's drugged. Then, as a minor one, Kirin will change depending on if you "kill" her during "marry, fuck, kill".

Assuming one goes complete red path here, we have a Kirin that offered to have a sexual relationship with Akira from the start, lost her virginity at a love hotel and had a threesome with Noriko - and that's it.

The green path Kirin has gone from offering a sexual relationship to Akira, to sexually assaulting/blackmailing Ayane, to losing her virginity at a love hotel, to preying on a drugged Miku, to going on a date with Akira to the sound of Ayane's song (despacito) after blackmailing her, to having the threesome with Noriko.

The green path Kirin has every reason to have her TSS. She is human garbage, she is a whore, she is a rapist, and all the things the people in the audience called her.

But what about red path Kirin? Sure, she offered to have sex with a teacher... and? If you went full red path she never blackmailed Ayane, thus she was not a rapist. She also never preyed on drugged Miku. How is this girl a monster exactly? She literally only had sex with one man, who she loves - and her roomate. So she danced to Ayane's song, but also so what? This Kirin never did anything bad to Ayane, in fact, dancing to her song is an appropriate revenge for losing the science fair. Is it because she fantasizes having sex with her sister? Or that she fantasizes with multiple women? I fail to see anything that merits this TSS.

So, in my humble opinion, once again, the red path barely makes sense. Also also, if you don't have sex with Haruka, there's just no TSS. So, in the full red path, Kirin is a girl that felt an inferiority complex towards her sister, sought sex with a teacher and then had a threesome with her roomate and said teacher. End of story. That's the entirety of her arc.

spoilers.title: Haruka situation
spoilers.html:
There is some dialogue, or rather narration, from this update which I think is pivotal in addressing what you talked about.

Haruka just had a regular upbringing, no real issues nor traumas, a happy marriage, until one day, because she felt very lonely for her husband being at war for years, she sought consolation at the arms of a man - and from there she started self-deprecating more and more into a bottomless hole.

If you don't have sex with Haruka, her entire arc stops at being selfish because "she felt so happy her husband was alive that she forgot to inquire about Maki's". That's it. I mean, sure, I get Maki being pissed - but let's be real, that's not the end of the world either. Cause she did feel like shit, and pursued Maki to apologise, including getting hit for it. And this, I remind you, is a Haruka that has zero self-deprecating issues. The Haruka that feels like shit because she misses her husband (and well, who wouldn't).

Why am I saying all of this though? Well, it's because the story Selebus is telling on the green path is one where Haruka never recovered from having cheated on her husband. That's the start of it all. To my eyes, it doesn't really matter to her if it's having sex with teenagers, or having sex in public, or becoming a sex slave, or just cheating - she lost herself regardless and is freefalling ever since.

I really like Haruka's story, and have since long ago. It's a pathetic character that merely lost herself entirely. If you all would remember, Haruka was missing because she almost lost her shop due to being witnessed having sex with Akira over the balcony. That's the character that on her next appearance tried to have sex with not one, but two teenagers and had to beg them both not to rat her out - all the while having other teenagers that WOULD have sex with her (Molly even having invited her previously)

If you look at the whole thing from up close it's a tragic story, but if you look at it from afar it's a comedy (which is also the blend that Selebus chooses when having her crashout on Akira, upon finding out that her husband is alive). Anyway, I do enjoy the story being told here and look forward to the next fall.

spoilers.title: Flawed Characters
spoilers.html:
I mostly agree with you. I think flawed characters are essential to a story, and I'm talking real flaws, not the sort of "my flaw is that I care too much about people" and protagonist shit like that. One of my favorite characters in LiL is Sara.

She is a deeply flawed character, but also captivating in what she tries to be despite her flaws. Her whole interaction with Ami during their trip, or even before, when they first meet at Akira's place is amazing. And yet, her flaws make sense. Because, if she tries so hard to be a good mother, because her parents sucked, and she was broken, then abandoned, then grieving - that's the exact same reason as to why she fails at being a "proper" mother.

She'd give the world to Sana, but she also can't stop drinking, or depending on her for being unable to move on from Shota's death. She doesn't want Sana to end up like her, so she finds herself unable to restrain her enough, and would even beg Akira to keep an eye on her. I don't think anyone would say Sara's arc is pathetic by any means. She has pathetic moments, and they're great, because they make so much sense with her history that it's inevitable.

Now, let's talk about Futaba. Her entire arc in this game is a history of aborted ideas. First there was the overweight thing, which resulted in nothing other than serving as plot for Yumi - remember the gym? yeah, nothingburger (again, other than stuff for Yumi, including Nodoka meeting Yuki there).

Then there was the eating disorder arc, which led to finding common ground with Imani (who also thinks of herself as a monster). And that led to... Futaba seeing herself as a monster in her TSS... Right. What about her eating disorder though? Nope, gone to the same place as the gym.

In the middle of all of this there was the Nodoka book arc, which Futaba grew really pissed about! Because she's. the. only. one. that. cares! She cares enough to be super pissed at Nodoka and stop talking to her! Until... Nodoka says she's not going to change at all and Futaba... accepts it because Nodoka says she likes her... Hmm... it gets worse.

There was also the "I have to protect Rin" arc. In which Futaba gets super pissed at Otoha! Because she should never have been allowed to treat Rin that way, and Futaba will protect Rin so that it never happens again. Until the same Otoha tells Futaba not to protect Rin and Futaba goes "well, I guess I gotta trust you, hope you're right"

And to finish it all off: "Futaba's parents" arc. Remember when she was angry at Akira for barging in her conversation with her mom? And that she was the perfect victim because she had no parents in the country, and she felt uglier than her classmates, and she shared an interest in literature with him? And then she confirmed all of what I just said because that's how she was portrayed in Nodoka's book more or less? Well, it gets worse for Futaba because amidst this all, she still has no parents around her! and then she stops hearing from them (oh no!). Do you know where this leads? You got it! Big Nothing Burger!

And if you count, you'll realise that three nothingburgers occur in the very same update, almost in the exact same conversation

I can't see this as being good writing. Regarding Chika, I think it's much simpler to talk about. It is plausible that she'd behave exactly as she did. No issues with the writing there, in fact it's working as intended because most people got really pissed at her, and I'm pretty sure that was the intended reaction.

Now, regarding my reaction personally, I'm just tired of her. Those years of her ignoring everything in her face really soured her character to me, and while the rabies Chika is technically a new arc, it is also a continuation of acting insane. Which she has been for years. I couldn't care less about the confession or the dumping that she did on Rin, I just wanted it to be over. Rin deserves way more - and instead she first gets Rika cockblocking her, and now Chika messing with her head. At least, she does not look at Chika the same way. So the harm could have been worse.

As per usual, I agree with essentially everything you mentioned.

And you are right that unfortunately there are a lot of inconsistencies in Sel's writing.
Ultimately, I believe it stems from his initial reluctancy to tell a kinetic story. He already made it clear that he intended the story to be told the way he wants to, but felt forced to indulge his players in giving them the option to diverge from certain paths, avoiding LIs and uncomfortable situations.
This, in turn, spiraled into a main story that, unless played exactly the way intended by the writer, is getting further and further riddled with plot holes, contradictive character behavior and missing content.
And we know that it can only get worse from here.

To top it off, as you mentioned, some story arcs turn out to be nothingburgers or, at the very least, seemingly conclude in unsatisfying ways that lack the expected narrative impact.
From what I remember him mentioning at times on Discord, it's most likely just him changing his mind or realizing he isn't able to wrap it up the way he intended to due to some other plot developments or new ideas he has and just drops it like a hot potato.

It isn't great, but to be fair to him, a VN isn't exactly a book. It's not a finished work of art that can be reviewed from beginning to end and adjusted with hindsight to polish it and tie up loose ends and fix some logical errors due to last minute changes to the story.
It's more comparable to TV shows in my opinion and how some of them have amazing first seasons, only to disappoint with later ones when it becomes apparent that the writers don't actually have good and creative ideas to close the loops within the plot and provide answers to the questions and conflicts that they themselves created (many such examples).

In that context, I'm still content with how Sel managed to keep the story plausible and relatively coherent, even despite those issues that mostly come from having differing story paths. Or at least to me it's easier to forgive him for that.
Because, on the topic of flawed characters, he might be the most flawed one of them all

spoilers.html:
I feel like it might be useful to highlight that there isn't ONE red path Kirin, but at least 9 worldlines of Kirins (not even considering her Karin permutations). I'll skip the "I think I actually love Akira" from last christmas, cause everyone should remember it, it's present in all timelines and I have a lot to cover.

So, to start with the permutations: Kirin can blackmail/sexually assault Ayane, which is the big one. Then, if Miku wins the Halloween contest, Kirin will also prey on her by having her compete against her in giving Akira a blowjob while she's drugged. Then, as a minor one, Kirin will change depending on if you "kill" her during "marry, fuck, kill".

Assuming one goes complete red path here, we have a Kirin that offered to have a sexual relationship with Akira from the start, lost her virginity at a love hotel and had a threesome with Noriko - and that's it.

The green path Kirin has gone from offering a sexual relationship to Akira, to sexually assaulting/blackmailing Ayane, to losing her virginity at a love hotel, to preying on a drugged Miku, to going on a date with Akira to the sound of Ayane's song (despacito) after blackmailing her, to having the threesome with Noriko.

The green path Kirin has every reason to have her TSS. She is human garbage, she is a whore, she is a rapist, and all the things the people in the audicience called her.

But what about red path Kirin? Sure, she offered to have sex with a teacher... and? If you went full red path she never blackmailed Ayane, thus she was not a rapist. She also never preyed on drugged Miku. How is this girl a monster exactly? She literally only had sex with one man, who she loves - and her roomate. So she danced to Ayane's song, but also so what? This Kirin never did anything bad to Ayane, in fact, dancing to her song is an appropriate revenge for losing the science fair. Is it because she fantasizes having sex with her sister? Or that she fantasizes with multiple women? I fail to see anything that merits this TSS.

So, in my humble opinion, once again, the red path barely makes sense. Also also, if you don't have sex with Haruka, there's just no TSS. So, in the full red path, Kirin is a girl that felt an inferiority complex towards her sister, sought sex with a teacher and then had a threesome with her roomate and said teacher. End of story. That's the entirety of her arc.

spoilers.title: Haruka situation
spoilers.html:
There is some dialogue, or rather narration, from this update which I think is pivotal in addressing what you talked about.

Haruka just had a regular upbringing, no real issues nor traumas, a happy marriage, until one day, because she felt very lonely for her husband being at war for years, she sought consolation at the arms of a man - and from there she started self-deprecating more and more into a bottomless hole.

If you don't have sex with Haruka, her entire arc stops at being selfish because "she felt so happy her husband was alive that she forgot to inquire about Maki's". That's it. I mean, sure, I get Maki being pissed - but let's be real, that's not the end of the world either. Cause she did feel like shit, and pursued Maki to apologise, including getting hit for it. And this, I remind you, is a Haruka that has zero self-deprecating issues. The Haruka that feels like shit because she misses her husband (and well, who wouldn't).

Why am I saying all of this though? Well, it's because the story Selebus is telling on the green path is one where Haruka never recovered from having cheated on her husband. That's the start of it all. To my eyes, it doesn't really matter to her if it's having sex with teenagers, or having sex in public, or becoming a sex slave, or just cheating - she lost herself regardless and is freefalling ever since.

I really like Haruka's story, and have since long ago. It's a pathetic character that merely lost herself entirely. If you all would remember, Haruka was missing because she almost lost her shop due to being witnessed having sex with Akira over the balcony. That's the character that on her next appearance tried to have sex with not one, but two teenagers and had to beg them both not to rat her out - all the while having other teenagers that WOULD have sex with her (Molly even having invited her previously)

If you look at the whole thing from up close it's a tragic story, but if you look at it from afar it's a comedy (which is also the blend that Selebus chooses when having her crashout on Akira, upon finding out that her husband is alive). Anyway, I do enjoy the story being told here and look forward to the next fall.

spoilers.title: Flawed Characters
spoilers.html:
I mostly agree with you. I think flawed characters are essential to a story, and I'm talking real flaws, not the sort of "my flaw is that I care too much about people" and protagonist shit like that. One of my favorite characters in LiL is Sara.

She is a deeply flawed character, but also captivating in what she tries to be despite her flaws. Her whole interaction with Ami during their trip, or even before, when they first meet at Akira's place is amazing. And yet, her flaws make sense. Because, if she tries so hard to be a good mother, because her parents sucked, and she was broken, then abandoned, then grieving - that's the exact same reason as to why she fails at being a "proper" mother.

She'd give the world to Sana, but she also can't stop drinking, or depending on her for being unable to move on from Shota's death. She doesn't want Sana to end up like her, so she finds herself unable to restrain her enough, and would even beg Akira to keep an eye on her. I don't think anyone would say Sara's arc is pathetic by any means. She has pathetic moments, and they're great, because they make so much sense with her history that it's inevitable.

Now, let's talk about Futaba. Her entire arc in this game is a history of aborted ideas. First there was the overweight thing, which resulted in nothing other than serving as plot for Yumi - remember the gym? yeah, nothingburger (again, other than stuff for Yumi, including Nodoka meeting Yuki there).

Then there was the eating disorder arc, which led to finding common ground with Imani (who also thinks of herself as a monster). And that led to... Futaba seeing herself as a monster in her TSS... Right. What about her eating disorder though? Nope, gone to the same place as the gym.

In the middle of all of this there was the Nodoka book arc, which Futaba grew really pissed about! Because she's. the. only. one. that. cares! She cares enough to be super pissed at Nodoka and stop talking to her! Until... Nodoka says she's not going to change at all and Futaba... accepts it because Nodoka says she likes her... Hmm... it gets worse.

There was also the "I have to protect Rin" arc. In which Futaba gets super pissed at Otoha! Because she should never have been allowed to treat Rin that way, and Futaba will protect Rin so that it never happens again. Until the same Otoha tells Futaba not to protect Rin and Futaba goes "well, I guess I gotta trust you, hope you're right"

And to finish it all off: "Futaba's parents" arc. Remember when she was angry at Akira for barging in her conversation with her mom? And that she was the perfect victim because she had no parents in the country, and she felt uglier than her classmates, and she shared an interest in literature with him? And then she confirmed all of what I just said because that's how she was portrayed in Nodoka's book more or less? Well, it gets worse for Futaba because amidst this all, she still has no parents around her! and then she stops hearing from them (oh no!). Do you know where this leads? You got it! Big Nothing Burger!

And if you count, you'll realise that three nothingburgers occur in the very same update, almost in the exact same conversation

I can't see this as being good writing. Regarding Chika, I think it's much simpler to talk about. It is plausible that she'd behave exactly as she did. No issues with the writing there, in fact it's working as intended because most people got really pissed at her, and I'm pretty sure that was the intended reaction.

Now, regarding my reaction personally, I'm just tired of her. Those years of her ignoring everything in her face really soured her character to me, and while the rabies Chika is technically a new arc, it is also a continuation of acting insane. Which she has been for years. I couldn't care less about the confession or the dumping that she did on Rin, I just wanted to be over. Rin deserves way more - and instead she first gets Rika cockblocking her, and now Chika messing with her head. At least, she does not look at Chika the same way. So the harm could have been worse.

Well… I did the last update yesterday, I took a day off because it gave me a migraine (happiness, that is, felicity!), and now I’m writing my review/analysis. Naturally, everything that follows is related, near or far, to the last update, so don’t click if you didn’t do it. Also, as a preamble, I want to say that I preferred it to 0.53. Really.

Anyway, no one, no two, get ready, the read will be long :

I’ll start with the character Nao who, we don’t present anymore, is still as strange as she is adorable and her (?) link with the character Maya, using this image :


And, I don’t know about you, but… it seems extremely related. The description of Maya’s farthest memory matches almost exactly how Nao was found. So, either it’s the way a wish appears in this universe (Maya is a wish, and Nao potentially one), or… her appearance echoes the way Maya appeared, binding them even more tightly. I can’t decide, I’m scared. Both explanations seem plausible.

Anyway, talking about Maya, I’ve got two or three things on her. First, because I have to :



Absolutely not.

With that settled, let’s move to the most interesting part. Because if Maya wasn’t «cock-block», I was!


AND NOTHING!!! AHHHHH!!!

Don’t give me false hopes like that, okay! It’s horrible! She was two fingers away from revealing everything, then… no. Sensei was no longer interested!
Why are you asking, seeing that she’s ready to tell you everything, and you change your mind like that?! Asshole! Sacripant! Veule!

Sorry…


To lighten my mood, I’d like to touch on the Kirin/Haruka case. Strange as it may be, I really liked it (I sternly condemn what Haruka did, of course, but from a narrative standpoint, that passage was well-crafted).

But not Sana’s betrayal.
I didn’t quite grasp it… she had a grievance against Kirin? I know Ayane did, but her? Even if Sana fantasizes about rape… she isn’t the one who’s raped (and she doesn’t even watch it!), so why?

No kidding, even now I wonder if it’s a «face-shifter» posing as her and triggering the following TPS. Seriously, I can’t explain it.

By the way, little aside, but the fact that Nao pulls Kirin out of her TPS with a slap… I don’t know. It’s both coherent and surprising.

Not to mention the shock when you wake up with that in front of you :

Anyway, Kirin/Haruka, then. The scene was perfectly disturbing, and Haruka’s pathos was… truly pathetic. Yet, without absolving her actions, this scene with Chika :
clearly shows the injustice of this world. Deep down, she’s right : why should Sensei get a pass (and be forgiven!), but not her?

Sure, she was much forceful than him (and to be fair, she HAS to initiate contact, whereas Sensei only has to pick up the slack). But beyond that, they’re both deviants.

And that’s why I even pray that the police catch her and arrest her. Already because it would illustrate Sensei’s impunity, and, more importantly, could potentially shift things up.

I’m worried, though, that her path is already set and she’s at high risk of joining the Yamaguchi clan.
Yeah. I’m serious. I have no proof of what I’m saying, but that’s what her character inspires me.

Also, to keep touching on Haruka a bit, the discussion with Maki and Sara perfectly illustrates why I don’t like talking to people:
Maki expresses concern, not about the dress code, but about the reason behind that attire: to seduce Sensei.

Then she tells Haruka that she surely wouldn’t have a relationship with a child if he tried to seduce her, to which Haruka replies: «What if that were the case?»

Beyond Haruka’s provocation and Maki’s snap reaction, Sara defends Haruka, saying she’s trying to be civilized…


Really?


REALLY?!


Girl, did you follow the discussion? Hopefully, she connected the dot after finding Haruka in the bathroom (right after Kirin fled), and urge her to go home…

So, sure, we don’t see Sara’s facial expression (maybe she was pitying her...), but I sincerely hope there was disdain and reproach.
I won’t comment on the dialogue’s coherence, because, even if it gives me goosebumps, it seemed way too natural…



Let's keep the adults a bit longer and talk a little about Touka and Tsubasa, and I’ve got «one» little gripe :

Strangely enough, maybe I’m misreading Touka’s character, but I’ve always seen her as smart and educated—especially on the political front. And there, her mother throws a purely political rhetoric, and she doesn’t even react! Even more, it’s the most worn-out rhetoric of all: «But why would we do that?»

At that moment I wanted to jump into the screen, slap Touka (she deserves it), and ask her mom: «And why wouldn’t you do it? What, morally, legally, TECHNICALLY, would stop you from doing it?»
Obviously I can’t do that (and even if I could, it wouldn’t have meant a thing), but hey… let me fantasize!


Now, let’s talk a bit about Chika/Rin, because… I think I fell in love with her. She’s far, far from my style… but this :
Oh damn, I loved it! I was as surprised as Rin, actually. Okay, pleasantly surprised, but you get the idea. That drama!

I know I talk about it a lot, but God, I love it! That’s why I liked this update more than the previous one, by the way. Aside from the final «betrayal» of Himawari, there were no other moments that strong. In my view, at least.

Also, to stay a bit more on Chika, the moment right after she learns that her friend’s mother has cancer, with the narrator saying: «And she did what any other girl of her age would do.»

My first thought was: «Is she cutting her veins?»

And the answer was: «Run to the bathroom to cry even more.»

At that precise instant, I realized that my friends might not be normal… because, yes, their first reflex was to cut their veins… my childhood, and theirs, was the most joyful (sarcasm).


Now, Nodoka.

Nodoka was both a pleasant surprise and a slight disappointment.
We learn first that she remembers the goth girl who helps Himawari :
Then that she’s «up-to-date» on the reset phenomenon:
For me, that’s a missed opportunity.

But before I explain why, here’s how I picture people looping back to their last line when we bring up the reset thing:
Everyone has, or had, a «failsafe» in their heads that flips on the moment someone nearby talks about resets—kind of like a tape-player that, when the tape jams, pulls back just a tad to free itself.
But that «failsafe,» as I see it, is mechanical; it’s not about knowing the loop, but about the loop itself.
So the reason Makoto or Ayane recall the loop is simply that the system no longer works.

And that’s why I feel this is a missed chance: it would’ve been great for Nodoka to intellectually spot the loop, yet still be unable to articulate it plainly.
That would explain her cryptic way of talking about the loop all this time, and would show her «vulnerability»: she sees that the loop exists, but she’s still bound to it.
An intellectual tragedy that I’d have found epic… but nope.

And for the good surprise:
Pure artistry.


And to wrap things up, Yasu God.
She makes it crystal-clear that Nozomu, who I still think is «HOPE,» is the creator of everything, all punctuated by «flashes» of Sensei being intimidated by his big brother Nozomu.

Is it a little presumptuous on my part to say that Sensei would be a god? I don’t think so, no. Especially with what Nodoka said earlier:

Frankly, it would make sense. Yeah, it would also read like a Greek myth... and now that I think about it, I’m convinced a ton of parallels could be drawn. But that’ll be for another time (maybe).
Phew… ~1,600 words according to LibreOffice. It was long, but I wanted to write. And looking at my work, I hope I’m not on anyone’s blacklist! That would be a shame for them to miss this.

Anyway, that’s all from me...

Oh, I almost forgot, Ami, one last word?
Sensei, I hate you, you know. She teases you and you don’t even notice.

And, finally… I vanish!

Let's keep the adults a bit longer and talk a little about Touka and Tsubasa, and I’ve got «one» little gripe :
Spoiler:
Politics
Strangely enough, maybe I’m misreading Touka’s character, but I’ve always seen her as smart and educated—especially on the political front. And there, her mother throws a purely political rhetoric, and she doesn’t even react! Even more, it’s the most worn-out rhetoric of all: «But why would we do that?»
At that moment I wanted to jump into the screen, slap Touka (she deserves it), and ask her mom: «And why wouldn’t you do it? What, morally, legally, TECHNICALLY, would stop you from doing it?»
Obviously I can’t do that (and even if I could, it wouldn’t have meant a thing), but hey… let me fantasize!
Now, let’s talk a bit about Chika/Rin, because… I think I fell in love with her. She’s far, far from my style… but this :
Spoiler:
Confession
Oh damn, I loved it! I was as surprised as Rin, actually. Okay, pleasantly surprised, but you get the idea. That drama!
I know I talk about it a lot, but God, I love it! That’s why I liked this update more than the previous one, by the way. Aside from the final «betrayal» of Himawari, there were no other moments that strong. In my view, at least.
Also, to stay a bit more on Chika, the moment right after she learns that her friend’s mother has cancer, with the narrator saying: «And she did what any other girl of her age would do.»
My first thought was: «Is she cutting her veins?»
And the answer was: «Run to the bathroom to cry even more.»
At that precise instant, I realized that my friends might not be normal… because, yes, their first reflex was to cut their veins… my childhood, and theirs, was the most joyful (sarcasm).
Now, Nodoka.
Nodoka was both a pleasant surprise and a slight disappointment.
We learn first that she remembers the goth girl who helps Himawari :
Spoiler:
So she remember
Then that she’s «up-to-date» on the reset phenomenon:
Spoiler:
So she knows
For me, that’s a missed opportunity.
But before I explain why, here’s how I picture people looping back to their last line when we bring up the reset thing:
Everyone has, or had, a «failsafe» in their heads that flips on the moment someone nearby talks about resets—kind of like a tape-player that, when the tape jams, pulls back just a tad to free itself.
But that «failsafe,» as I see it, is mechanical; it’s not about knowing the loop, but about the loop itself.
So the reason Makoto or Ayane recall the loop is simply that the system no longer works.
And that’s why I feel this is a missed chance: it would’ve been great for Nodoka to intellectually spot the loop, yet still be unable to articulate it plainly.
That would explain her cryptic way of talking about the loop all this time, and would show her «vulnerability»: she sees that the loop exists, but she’s still bound to it.
An intellectual tragedy that I’d have found epic… but nope.
And for the good surprise:
Spoiler:
Mother?
Pure artistry.
And to wrap things up,
Yasu
God.
She makes it crystal-clear that Nozomu, who I still think is «HOPE,» is the creator of everything, all punctuated by «flashes» of Sensei being intimidated by his big brother Nozomu.
Is it a little presumptuous on my part to say that Sensei would be a god? I don’t think so, no. Especially with what Nodoka said earlier:
Spoiler:
Become a gods
Frankly, it would make sense. Yeah, it would also read like a Greek myth... and now that I think about it, I’m convinced a ton of parallels could be drawn. But that’ll be for another time (maybe).
Phew… ~1,600 words according to LibreOffice. It was long, but I wanted to write. And looking at my work, I hope I’m not on anyone’s blacklist! That would be a shame for them to miss this.
Anyway, that’s all from me...
Oh, I almost forgot, Ami, one last word?
Spoiler:
Ami
Sensei, I hate you, you know. She teases you and you don’t even notice.
And, finally… I vanish!

I will replay the game sometime in the near future but since I don't remember much I want to ask and clarify some of the big things so I have a solid enough foundation to start.

Let us start with the most basic of information and work out way up with more obscure stuff.

1)Sensei's name is Akira. The name had a huge reveal event that also revealed sekai which was incredible.
2)The world that we currently reside in is called Terminal 23. There have been a looot of theories and speculations about other terminals but I think it has been confirmed that Terminal 22 has been terminated Don't quote me though.
3) The upside down house and it's residents exist,sadly.
4)The 3 major gods that matter are the 3C gods:Callous Calm and Concerned.
Calm is Wires. Which fits not only with his personality of not needlessly intervening with the world and it's residents but also with his belief to conserve the status quo. he had a whole event round that which was pretty cool and clear cut.

Callous is hope. Don't think this was ever stated outright like with wires but I think everybody can agree that possessing a sick schizophrenic girl and making her scream "YOU MUST TAKE WHAT FOESNT BELONG TO YOU YOU FISGUSTING FILTHY PIECE OF TRASH" and other such compliments(Is this flirting?) isn't the most sensitive thing. Also there's this whole rebirth and retribution thing going on that Yasu has been preaching which to my knowledge Hope never said or preached any of this madness Infront of us but eh.

Pareidolia is concerned. Now pareidolia himself has talked about how concerned he is and yada yada but I find this to be really funny and really paradoxical. Like he acts like he cares and is concerned but then goes full throttle and wants Akira to continue the cycle and corrupt everything around him which is hilariously paradoxical. Now I think he plant d a seed inside Sana that has and hopefully is continuing to bloom but there's one thing that puzzles me about him. Just before he disappeared he supposedly did something to help Akira,Akira called him out saying that all this is just a manipulation attempt by him and then pareidolia had a mask off moment. Apologies for how scatterbrained this is but it was a pretty weird event to me since Im not sure if it's that simple. Like yes pareidolia is just this irredeemable being that just wants to cause as much pain and suffering to Akira and Co or if there's something bigger.

5)Sekais whole story is something I remember quite clearly. She groomed Akira,even wrote poems about it which was an incredible arc,with Wakana slowly finding out about it and whatnot.Also Nodoka calling him Aki-kun and sending him into a coma was hot and also very tragic.Anyways tldr sekai groomed Akira,car crash killed both her and nozumo,his brother,He adopted Ami and the rest is history.Thankfully I remember the whole Maya grooming thing but I'm not sure about the overall time line.

Was it Akira hangs out with the Nakarayamas with sekai alive>He finds the cat and adopts her>grooming.jpeg>Sekai dies>Akira cuts contact with the Nakarayamas and adopts Ami.

6)Maya prime is gone and replaced by essentially a mind wiped Maya that we keep having sex with. I remember some of the big brains here talking a out and implied heaven or the wishing well itself being the place where Maya prime is and that we,in the future will be able to bring her back but I don't remember the details.

7)Himawari is trying to break the cycles? Help everyone escape the simulation? What her endgoal is doesn't really matter since we know for sure that she wasn't all of this to end,no matter what "this" is. Also she is using tsubasa and I think someone else as aides,which is cool.

8)Ami.Ami has become the most important character for a while imo. Starting with the theory that moonflarr first brought up with Ami having knowledge of past resets,Ami being able to communicate or at least sense sekai(Weren't there 2?),the whole bus event,the reset where she gutted Nodoka like a fish(Nice) and plenty others. I could go on and on but you get the idea. Ami is important and we NEED to pay attention to her.

...She is also cute.

This is pretty much what I remember from the BIG lore details.

Now I will briefly mention some lesser lore bits that hopefully have been answered or concluded in some way.

Yumi is known by another name by pareidolia.

Literally everything to do with the upside down house.

Yukis cancer arc.

Akiras relationship with the Nakayama's.

Sara's deal with Pegasus.

Honestly I think that's it.I may haveissed some interpersonal drama between the characters but ehhhh I'll rember it someday when I replay.


I am shamelessly begging for you guys to briefly tell me if my recollection of the games events as of...whatever version the Nozumo pissing on Akira eventually was is correct,if it's missing anything important or needed to understand future stuff etc etc.

If I'm good then I'll just continue on from that point and be happy,if not replay from 0 it is. Thank you in advance anons.

Calm is Wires. Which fits not only with his personality of not needlessly intervening with the world and it's residents but also with his belief to conserve the status quo. he had a whole event round that which was pretty cool and clear cut.
Callous is hope. Don't think this was ever stated outright like with wires but I think everybody can agree that possessing a sick schizophrenic girl and making her scream "YOU MUST TAKE WHAT FOESNT BELONG TO YOU YOU FISGUSTING FILTHY PIECE OF TRASH" and other such compliments(Is this flirting?) isn't the most sensitive thing. Also there's this whole rebirth and retribution thing going on that Yasu has been preaching which to my knowledge Hope never said or preached any of this madness Infront of us but eh.

posts.content_html_raw:
Well, having already covered the part where I can't really care about Chika as I once did due to fatigue, I'll say this:
I have seen both examples of what she did in real life, especially in my younger years. What I saw in the update, and what Selebus seems to have intended. And they are different things with similar executions.

In one example, you mess up what you're doing but ultimately you're motivated by genuine care about the other person. A sort of "you deserve better than what I am right now, and I just can't add shit to your life". In the other, you just dump all over the person, convincing yourself you're sacrificing yourself for them, when in fact you're just trauma dumping and sefishly convincing yourself you're some kind of martyr for it.

I think Selebus aimed for the first and came out with the second. Chika, as was written in that scene (to me) seems much more worried about the fact that the person she is now can't be with Rin (thus self-interest), than the idea that the person she's right now won't add to Rin's life in a positive way. Her entire speech is about how she has to fix herself before coming back to Rin, whereas a person that really cared wouldn't even consider "coming back to Rin", in fact, such a person wouldn't even dump all of this on her.

The "messing things up" part I mentioned addresses some of this, because she's not acting in an optimal way. But that does not excuse the truth of the matter coming out when we can't emotionally put up with creating a narrative to justify our actions. What she says are her raw emotions. And her raw emotions are that she wants Rin, but she knows that as she is right now she has no chance, so instead she trauma dumps, tries to come out as a martyr, and doesn't even want to give Rin a chance to logically dismantle this idiocy.
That Selebus thinks this is growth is ridiculous to me. Chika's growth was in her previous event, her "violent sadness" was the first event in years that I truly enjoyed Chika as a character, it was amazing. But this missed the mark SO BAD based on what he wanted to convey, and what he actually wrote.

Moonflare said:
Well, having already covered the part where I can't really care about Chika as I once did due to fatigue, I'll say this:
I have seen both examples of what she did in real life, especially in my younger years. What I saw in the update, and what Selebus seems to have intended. And they are different things with similar executions.

In one example, you mess up what you're doing but ultimately you're motivated by genuine care about the other person. A sort of "you deserve better than what I am right now, and I just can't add shit to your life". In the other, you just dump all over the person, convincing yourself you're sacrificing yourself for them, when in fact you're just trauma dumping and sefishly convincing yourself you're some kind of martyr for it.

I think Selebus aimed for the first and came out with the second. Chika, as was written in that scene (to me) seems much more worried about the fact that the person she is now can't be with Rin (thus self-interest), than the idea that the person she's right now won't add to Rin's life in a positive way. Her entire speech is about how she has to fix herself before coming back to Rin, whereas a person that really cared wouldn't even consider "coming back to Rin", in fact, such a person wouldn't even dump all of this on her.

The "messing things up" part I mentioned addresses some of this, because she's not acting in an optimal way. But that does not excuse the truth of the matter coming out when we can't emotionally put up with creating a narrative to justify our actions. What she says are her raw emotions. And her raw emotions are that she wants Rin, but she knows that as she is right now she has no chance, so instead she trauma dumps, tries to come out as a martyr, and doesn't even want to give Rin a chance to logically dismantle this idiocy.
That Selebus thinks this is growth is ridiculous to me. Chika's growth was in her previous event, her "violent sadness" was the first event in years that I truly enjoyed Chika as a character, it was amazing. But this missed the mark SO BAD based on what he wanted to convey, and what he actually wrote.
Click to expand...
Being motivated by self-interest is good, though. Yes, Chika is cutting contact with Rin for herself, and no, she isn't trying to make it out as self-sacrifice and I have no idea where are you getting that idea from. She is literally losing her mind because of love, realizing that and bailing is character growth compared to all the times her love lead her into an awful situation. Rin and relationship with Rin is very much secondary to her right now, and there's absolutely nothing in her speech about "coming back after she's better".

Edit: Oh, don't tell me you're reading "And sometimes, you need to sacrifice something you love if it means protecting everything else" as Chika saying is self-sacrificing? Because it's literally the opposite, she is saying "Yes, Rin, I am sacrificing you and your feelings on the altar of protecting the rest of my life. I know you're strong enough to handle that". And it's not exactly good or fair to Rin, but that's how it is sometimes.

John Smith V said:
Can anyone can tell me if the events of this epic story are explained somewhere?
Click to expand...
Lessons in Love entire story so far:
Our protagonist is a man called Akira that was abused by his brother since a young age and then saved by his brother's girlfriend. Nozomu stopped directly tormenting him from then on, but Sekai, the one that saved him, started sexually assaulting him and did so for years until her death. Because she was also his savior, this fucked up his mind and sexuality into distorting his ideas of love, and grooming him into another predator like her.

When Sekai died in a car accident along with Nozomu, Akira loses his world and has to create his own worldview for the first time, but by then he's already an adult and is unable to cope. He distances himself from his girlfriend at the time, a girl called Niki, cause he wouldn't subject her to a life with him. In his desperation, he wishes for someone that could understand him and with whom he could indulge in his distorted sexuality but in a healthy way, unlike what he had with Sekai.

The impossible wish comes true in the form of a girl standing alone in the rain, without a past other than also the vague idea of being abused, and the quick will to start a romantic relationship with him, while being a kid. Starting from her and being at his age and mentality (from when he met Sekai), this is the redo of what he had with Sekai in a "healthy" capacity. That's the story of Maya and Akira.

Akira then adopts Ami, the child of Nozomu and Sekai, and possibily his. But, even though Maya exists in his life, he's unable to function properly, just barely hanging on. This leads to Ami having to deal with her parents' death and a non-functional guardian. She adapts by creating a mentality of the two of them being the only people in the world that understand eachother, having the same trauma, and develops the idea that rather than Akira being her own world, she's the guardian of a world made just for the two of them - that she has to protect even from him.

Fast-forward and Akira is around 30 years old, about 6-7 years after the accident. He has dated Maya for all that time and was faithful to her. For example, never developing a sexual relationship with Ami, although she had tried to many times. At some point, it is assumed that he kills himself by jumping off the school building. Maya, a wish of his own, makes a wish that involves bringing him back to life - and, although it shouldn't be possible for wishes to make wishes, it comes true in a distorted way.

Maya is then subjected to thousands of years in an ever repeating reality of her current year of highschool by the time she made her wish. All of her classmates also repeat that year, and although there is an Akira, it's not her Akira. But a copy made from her wish. A company that oversees these alternate realities marvels at how it was possible for this anomaly to happen, and start investigating Maya's world, also known as TERMINAL 23. These employees take the form of both caretakers (entities that correct the world with the end of each cycle), and gods (employees of the company that are capable of granting wishes by forming contracts with humans).

Such a long time passes during this observation that the company starts allowing just about anything to figure out what the anomaly is. This starts to take form in creative forms of psychological torture centered around Maya and her fake Akira, but nothing results in anything of value. A secondary anomaly also takes place in the form of the Ami of this reality, which somehow becomes protected from lasting interference by both caretakers and the highest ranking of gods. It is then that the game starts, by the actual Akira that made the wish for Maya being transported to her world.

This Akira, however, barely has any memories and believes he's a random person in the body of some teacher, here to live out the dreams of a harem game without consequences. With time, and by interacting with his students, alongside Maya and Ami (that either knows some stuff but doesn't believe it's him, or that knows all the stuff but isn't interested in sharing) he starts recalling memories of "the body". This goes on until he realises that what he's recalling are his actual memories. And that he's Akira Arakawa.

Akira and Maya get closer even faster due to the interference of a mysterious entity that both shows up from time to time, and that often talks to Akira through narration. Maya starts to believe this is not a copy of Akira, but her actual Akira. Though she doesn't recall that either she's a wish, nor that this world is her creation. She's also in a situation where getting too close to him might break him, due to the experiments made by the gods in order to understand the nature of this world.

Through their journeys to understand the nature of this world, a girl named Ayane also starts to remember the resets and show up at the rooftop. Maya dismisses it as a random anomaly that won't last, having already happened before - but Ayane eventually becomes a lasting part of the group also through the interference of the mysterious entity that personally meets up with her to save her.

All the while, three different gods have been interacting with Akira - HOPE, Wires and Pareidolia. They are also known as Users 1, 2 and 3. And have employees/freelancers (Moyo, Long Maya, and others) that work with either one from time to time, and also spokespeople (like Yasu, Tsuneyo and Kaori). Akira interprets their interactions in multiple ways, even though, at the end of the day, things are much simpler than they appear - all of them just being employees at a company trying to understand this world/amusing themselves with it.

By the end of chapter 3, Maya is taken from him. She's replaced with a new Maya, throwing Akira into a deep state of depression - being the second time the love of his life dies in front of him. Ami starts showing the truth of what she really is by then, by closing Akira off from any contact with the rest of this world and creating their own bubble (that she marvels at). During this time, however, other gods that work with the company start directly interfering as well (having given the go-ahead because of some sort of event). One of them (Gossamer) is directly responsible for helping Akira get back to his life with his own permission.

Without Maya, Akira is even more passive than he ever was - and Ayane takes front-stage in trying to figure things out. Pareidolia, the third god, reveals himself as being the one that met Akira as a kid and that somehow was fished out of oblivion back to him by forces unknown. He declares that his gung-ho attitude towards him was actually conforming to what he needed from him, and that he actually cares deeply about Akira (being concerned). The extent of how much of this is truth is unknown, but Pareidolia does reveal a lot to Akira about the nature of the gods, and even some of his friends (like Kaori and the remnants of Sekai that haunt him and possess her).

The constant interference of different gods continues messing with his life and he sinks ever down into being passive and aimless. That's when the mysterious narrator starts showing up again, either to help Ayane or him. Ayane is able to recall the narrator from their previous encounters, and names her: Himawari. She sends them to an alternate reality in order to shield them until she can restore their world, which is on the brink of being erased, rather than reset.

In this different reality they come to confirm that Himawari (the name of Akira's favorite flower) is their daughter. They relive her memories/simulation of her perfect life with them, and are imbued with their future feelings towards the daughter they're bound to have. Akira, for the first time in his life, comes to know what real love and happiness are. Through the patterns of the body he's inhabiting (his future self) he's able to come to terms with everything he has been searching for and yet didn't know existed. This makes him able to put aside all of his trauma for the good of his daughter (and through her, also of his wife).

They are pulled out of this reality however, and Himawari reveals yet more about the company she also works in, and this reality, Ami and Maya. Himawari's plan and reasoning for joining the company was to achieve an objective of being able to transport people between worlds, towards multiple happy endings that they could visit on and off. A future filled with all the best outcomes for everyone, where no one is unhappy. She also wished to help her parents throughout what was the most difficult stage of their lives and make things easier to them. But her interference this time (even though she was always breaking the rules) was just too much - and she has to go away and just watch from here on.

As Shiori (a veteran caretaker) assumes her position in correcting things in Maya's world, Himawari has to erase Akira and Ayane's memories of her, just leaving all the rest of the information she has granted them. Wishing for their reunion, she leaves them and that's where we're now. Akira has a newfound obssession with reuniting with his daughter, even though the memories of what brought this are hazy. The same goes for Ayane.

This makes our protagonist make different decisions regarding his previous status as a sex toy for all the girls, prioritizing investigating Maya, Ami and the world itself (while still using sex as a coping mechanism on the side). We've also come to know that Sekai is present in this world as an entity called "The World Itself", and that HOPE is likely Nozomu (Akira's brother). Or rather, it's also likely that both of them are reflections of how Akira saw them when Maya created this world for him.

This and more mysteries are what lies ahead, as we move forward towards the ending of the harem route and the mysteries that are likely to start the dark route. Then we'll finally get Himawari's own wish of the purity routes. And eventually the true ending of the game.
Regarding the conclusion, we're just past the halfway point of the story.

So, maybe somewhere around 2030. Do mind that it's 2030 for the true ending, so the first ending should come much earlier. It's ending of the harem arc (where we're at), dark route, purity routes and true end. Each purity route serves as an ending already, kind of like Ayane's epilogue but a redo of the entire game for a specific girl so, conceivably, one can stop there.

Our protagonist is a man called Akira that was abused by his brother since a young age and then saved by his brother's girlfriend. Nozomu stopped directly tormenting him from then on, but Sekai, the one that saved him, started sexually assaulting him and did so for years until her death. Because she was also his savior, this fucked up his mind and sexuality into distorting his ideas of love, and grooming him into another predator like her.
When Sekai died in a car accident along with Nozomu, Akira loses his world and has to create his own worldview for the first time, but by then he's already an adult and is unable to cope. He distances himself from his girlfriend at the time, a girl called Niki, cause he wouldn't subject her to a life with him. In his desperation, he wishes for someone that could understand him and with whom he could indulge in his distorted sexuality but in a healthy way, unlike what he had with Sekai.
The impossible wish comes true in the form of a girl standing alone in the rain, without a past other than also the vague idea of being abused, and the quick will to start a romantic relationship with him, while being a kid. Starting from her and being at his age and mentality (from when he met Sekai), this is the redo of what he had with Sekai in a "healthy" capacity. That's the story of Maya and Akira.
Akira then adopts Ami, the child of Nozomu and Sekai, and possibily his. But, even though Maya exists in his life, he's unable to function properly, just barely hanging on. This leads to Ami having to deal with her parents' death and a non-functional guardian. She adapts by creating a mentality of the two of them being the only people in the world that understand eachother, having the same trauma, and develops the idea that rather than Akira being her own world, she's the guardian of a world made just for the two of them - that she has to protect even from him.
Fast-forward and Akira is around 30 years old, about 6-7 years after the accident. He has dated Maya for all that time and was faithful to her. For example, never developing a sexual relationship with Ami, although she had tried to many times. At some point, it is assumed that he kills himself by jumping off the school building. Maya, a wish of his own, makes a wish that involves bringing him back to life - and, although it shouldn't be possible for wishes to make wishes, it comes true in a distorted way.
Maya is then subjected to thousands of years in an ever repeating reality of her current year of highschool by the time she made her wish. All of her classmates also repeat that year, and although there is an Akira, it's not her Akira. But a copy made from her wish. A company that oversees these alternate realities marvels at how it was possible for this anomaly to happen, and start investigating Maya's world, also known as TERMINAL 23. These employees take the form of both caretakers (entities that correct the world with the end of each cycle), and gods (employees of the company that are capable of granting wishes by forming contracts with humans).
Such a long time passes during this observation that the company starts allowing just about anything to figure out what the anomaly is. This starts to take form in creative forms of psychological torture centered around Maya and her fake Akira, but nothing results in anything of value. A secondary anomaly also takes place in the form of the Ami of this reality, which somehow becomes protected from lasting interference by both caretakers and the highest ranking of gods. It is then that the game starts, by the actual Akira that made the wish for Maya being transported to her world.
This Akira, however, barely has any memories and believes he's a random person in the body of some teacher, here to live out the dreams of a harem game without consequences. With time, and by interacting with his students, alongside Maya and Ami (that either knows some stuff but doesn't believe it's him, or that knows all the stuff but isn't interested in sharing) he starts recalling memories of "the body". This goes on until he realises that what he's recalling are his actual memories. And that he's Akira Arakawa.
Akira and Maya get closer even faster due to the interference of a mysterious entity that both shows up from time to time, and that often talks to Akira through narration. Maya starts to believe this is not a copy of Akira, but her actual Akira. Though she doesn't recall that either she's a wish, nor that this world is her creation. She's also in a situation where getting too close to him might break him, due to the experiments made by the gods in order to understand the nature of this world.
Through their journeys to understand the nature of this world, a girl named Ayane also starts to remember the resets and show up at the rooftop. Maya dismisses it as a random anomaly that won't last, having already happened before - but Ayane eventually becomes a lasting part of the group also through the interference of the mysterious entity that personally meets up with her to save her.
All the while, three different gods have been interacting with Akira - HOPE, Wires and Pareidolia. They are also known as Users 1, 2 and 3. And have employees/freelancers (Moyo, Long Maya, and others) that work with either one from time to time, and also spokespeople (like Yasu, Tsuneyo and Kaori). Akira interprets their interactions in multiple ways, even though, at the end of the day, things are much simpler than they appear - all of them just being employees at a company trying to understand this world/amusing themselves with it.
By the end of chapter 3, Maya is taken from him. She's replaced with a new Maya, throwing Akira into a deep state of depression - being the second time the love of his life dies in front of him. Ami starts showing the truth of what she really is by then, by closing Akira off from any contact with the rest of this world and creating their own bubble (that she marvels at). During this time, however, other gods that work with the company start directly interfering as well (having given the go-ahead because of some sort of event). One of them (Gossamer) is directly responsible for helping Akira get back to his life with his own permission.
Without Maya, Akira is even more passive than he ever was - and Ayane takes front-stage in trying to figure things out. Pareidolia, the third god, reveals himself as being the one that met Akira as a kid and that somehow was fished out of oblivion back to him by forces unknown. He declares that his gung-ho attitude towards him was actually conforming to what he needed from him, and that he actually cares deeply about Akira (being concerned). The extent of how much of this is truth is unknown, but Pareidolia does reveal a lot to Akira about the nature of the gods, and even some of his friends (like Kaori and the remnants of Sekai that haunt him and possess her).
The constant interference of different gods continues messing with his life and he sinks ever down into being passive and aimless. That's when the mysterious narrator starts showing up again, either to help Ayane or him. Ayane is able to recall the narrator from their previous encounters, and names her: Himawari. She sends them to an alternate reality in order to shield them until she can restore their world, which is on the brink of being erased, rather than reset.
In this different reality they come to confirm that Himawari (the name of Akira's favorite flower) is their daughter. They relive her memories/simulation of her perfect life with them, and are imbued with their future feelings towards the daughter they're bound to have. Akira, for the first time in his life, comes to know what real love and happiness are. Through the patterns of the body he's inhabiting (his future self) he's able to come to terms with everything he has been searching for and yet didn't know existed. This makes him able to put aside all of his trauma for the good of his daughter (and through her, also of his wife).
They are pulled out of this reality however, and Himawari reveals yet more about the company she also works in, and this reality, Ami and Maya. Himawari's plan and reasoning for joining the company was to achieve an objective of being able to transport people between worlds, towards multiple happy endings that they could visit on and off. A future filled with all the best outcomes for everyone, where no one is unhappy. She also wished to help her parents throughout what was the most difficult stage of their lives and make things easier to them. But her interference this time (even though she was always breaking the rules) was just too much - and she has to go away and just watch from here on.
As Shiori (a veteran caretaker) assumes her position in correcting things in Maya's world, Himawari has to erase Akira and Ayane's memories of her, just leaving all the rest of the information she has granted them. Wishing for their reunion, she leaves them and that's where we're now. Akira has a newfound obssession with reuniting with his daughter, even though the memories of what brought this are hazy. The same goes for Ayane.
This makes our protagonist make different decisions regarding his previous status as a sex toy for all the girls, prioritizing investigating Maya, Ami and the world itself (while still using sex as a coping mechanism on the side). We've also come to know that Sekai is present in this world as an entity called "The World Itself", and that HOPE is likely Nozomu (Akira's brother). Or rather, it's also likely that both of them are reflections of how Akira saw them when Maya created this world for him.
This and more mysteries are what lies ahead, as we move forward towards the ending of the harem route and the mysteries that are likely to start the dark route. Then we'll finally get Himawari's own wish of the purity routes. And eventually the true ending of the game.
Regarding the conclusion, we're just past the halfway point of the story.
So, maybe somewhere around 2030. Do mind that it's 2030 for the true ending, so the first ending should come much earlier. It's ending of the harem arc (where we're at), dark route, purity routes and true end. Each purity route serves as an ending already, kind of like Ayane's epilogue but a redo of the entire game for a specific girl so, conceivably, one can stop there.

Maya starts to believe this is not a copy of Akira, but her actual Akira. Though she doesn't recall that either she's a wish, nor that this world is her creation. She's also in a situation where getting too close to him might break him, due to the experiments made by the gods in order to understand the nature of this world.

Through their journeys to understand the nature of this world, a girl named Ayane also starts to remember the resets and show up at the rooftop. Maya dismisses it as a random anomaly that won't last, having already happened before - but Ayane eventually becomes a lasting part of the group also through the interference of the mysterious entity that personally meets up with her to save her.

All the while, three different gods have been interacting with Akira - HOPE, Wires and Pareidolia. They are also known as Users 1, 2 and 3. And have employees/freelancers (Moyo, Long Maya, and others) that work with either one from time to time, and also spokespeople (like Yasu, Tsuneyo and Kaori). Akira interprets their interactions in multiple ways, even though, at the end of the day, things are much simpler than they appear - all of them just being employees at a company trying to understand this world/amusing themselves with it.

By the end of chapter 3, Maya is taken from him. She's replaced with a new Maya, throwing Akira into a deep state of depression - being the second time the love of his life dies in front of him. Ami starts showing the truth of what she really is by then, by closing Akira off from any contact with the rest of this world and creating their own bubble (that she marvels at). During this time, however, other gods that work with the company start directly interfering as well (having given the go-ahead because of some sort of event). One of them (Gossamer) is directly responsible for helping Akira get back to his life with his own permission.

Without Maya, Akira is even more passive than he ever was - and Ayane takes front-stage in trying to figure things out. Pareidolia, the third god, reveals himself as being the one that met Akira as a kid and that somehow was fished out of oblivion back to him by forces unknown. He declares that his gung-ho attitude towards him was actually conforming to what he needed from him, and that he actually cares deeply about Akira (being concerned). The extent of how much of this is truth is unknown, but Pareidolia does reveal a lot to Akira about the nature of the gods, and even some of his friends (like Kaori and the remnants of Sekai that haunt him and possess her).

The constant interference of different gods continues messing with his life and he sinks ever down into being passive and aimless. That's when the mysterious narrator starts showing up again, either to help Ayane or him. Ayane is able to recall the narrator from their previous encounters, and names her: Himawari. She sends them to an alternate reality in order to shield them until she can restore their world, which is on the brink of being erased, rather than reset.

In this different reality they come to confirm that Himawari (the name of Akira's favorite flower) is their daughter. They relive her memories/simulation of her perfect life with them, and are imbued with their future feelings towards the daughter they're bound to have. Akira, for the first time in his life, comes to know what real love and happiness are. Through the patterns of the body he's inhabiting (his future self) he's able to come to terms with everything he has been searching for and yet didn't know existed. This makes him able to put aside all of his trauma for the good of his daughter (and through her, also of his wife).

They are pulled out of this reality however, and Himawari reveals yet more about the company she also works in, and this reality, Ami and Maya. Himawari's plan and reasoning for joining the company was to achieve an objective of being able to transport people between worlds, towards multiple happy endings that they could visit on and off. A future filled with all the best outcomes for everyone, where no one is unhappy. She also wished to help her parents throughout what was the most difficult stage of their lives and make things easier to them. But her interference this time (even though she was always breaking the rules) was just too much - and she has to go away and just watch from here on.

As Shiori (a veteran caretaker) assumes her position in correcting things in Maya's world, Himawari has to erase Akira and Ayane's memories of her, just leaving all the rest of the information she has granted them. Wishing for their reunion, she leaves them and that's where we're now. Akira has a newfound obssession with reuniting with his daughter, even though the memories of what brought this are hazy. The same goes for Ayane.

This makes our protagonist make different decisions regarding his previous status as a sex toy for all the girls, prioritizing investigating Maya, Ami and the world itself (while still using sex as a coping mechanism on the side). We've also come to know that Sekai is present in this world as an entity called "The World Itself", and that HOPE is likely Nozomu (Akira's brother). Or rather, it's also likely that both of them are reflections of how Akira saw them when Maya created this world for him.

This and more mysteries are what lies ahead, as we move forward towards the ending of the harem route and the mysteries that are likely to start the dark route. Then we'll finally get Himawari's own wish of the purity routes. And eventually the true ending of the game.
Regarding the conclusion, we're just past the halfway point of the story.

So, maybe somewhere around 2030. Do mind that it's 2030 for the true ending, so the first ending should come much earlier. It's ending of the harem arc (where we're at), dark route, purity routes and true end. Each purity route serves as an ending already, kind of like Ayane's epilogue but a redo of the entire game for a specific girl so, conceivably, one can stop there.

Pareidolia, the third god, reveals himself as being the one that met Akira as a kid and that somehow was fished out of oblivion back to him by forces unknown. He declares that his gung-ho attitude towards him was actually conforming to what he needed from him, and that he actually cares deeply about Akira (being concerned). The extent of how much of this is truth is unknown, but Pareidolia does reveal a lot to Akira about the nature of the gods, and even some of his friends (like Kaori and the remnants of Sekai that haunt him and possess her).
The constant interference of different gods continues messing with his life and he sinks ever down into being passive and aimless. That's when the mysterious narrator starts showing up again, either to help Ayane or him. Ayane is able to recall the narrator from their previous encounters, and names her: Himawari. She sends them to an alternate reality in order to shield them until she can restore their world, which is on the brink of being erased, rather than reset.
In this different reality they come to confirm that Himawari (the name of Akira's favorite flower) is their daughter. They relive her memories/simulation of her perfect life with them, and are imbued with their future feelings towards the daughter they're bound to have. Akira, for the first time in his life, comes to know what real love and happiness are. Through the patterns of the body he's inhabiting (his future self) he's able to come to terms with everything he has been searching for and yet didn't know existed. This makes him able to put aside all of his trauma for the good of his daughter (and through her, also of his wife).
They are pulled out of this reality however, and Himawari reveals yet more about the company she also works in, and this reality, Ami and Maya. Himawari's plan and reasoning for joining the company was to achieve an objective of being able to transport people between worlds, towards multiple happy endings that they could visit on and off. A future filled with all the best outcomes for everyone, where no one is unhappy. She also wished to help her parents throughout what was the most difficult stage of their lives and make things easier to them. But her interference this time (even though she was always breaking the rules) was just too much - and she has to go away and just watch from here on.
As Shiori (a veteran caretaker) assumes her position in correcting things in Maya's world, Himawari has to erase Akira and Ayane's memories of her, just leaving all the rest of the information she has granted them. Wishing for their reunion, she leaves them and that's where we're now. Akira has a newfound obssession with reuniting with his daughter, even though the memories of what brought this are hazy. The same goes for Ayane.
This makes our protagonist make different decisions regarding his previous status as a sex toy for all the girls, prioritizing investigating Maya, Ami and the world itself (while still using sex as a coping mechanism on the side). We've also come to know that Sekai is present in this world as an entity called "The World Itself", and that HOPE is likely Nozomu (Akira's brother). Or rather, it's also likely that both of them are reflections of how Akira saw them when Maya created this world for him.
This and more mysteries are what lies ahead, as we move forward towards the ending of the harem route and the mysteries that are likely to start the dark route. Then we'll finally get Himawari's own wish of the purity routes. And eventually the true ending of the game.

Comiies said:
Maya, wishing well and gods?
Click to expand...
The following is mostly supposition based on what we do know.
We have no further details involving wishes or Maya. Regarding the Wishing Well, it is a place, like a nexus of realities, where you can go from one place to another.

From my understanding, gods don't exist solely within the company, but have always been around, utilizing the wishing well to perform wishes. Think gods in the sense of Japanese mythology, not ours. So if someone starts praying for good wind, a god of wind is born as a result of this worship. That god has access to the wishing well, and can use it to grant that prayer. In this sense, gods have always been born all the time for the simplest reasons, aka prayers, aka wishes.

A point of note is that there seems to be a safety net in the universe, where a wish will not be granted to the person that made the wish (since it all these wishes were actually altering current reality, reality would break). Instead, the god will grant said wish to another version of the person that made it, in a reality where that wish has always been reality - thus, preventing any imbalance with their respective worlds.

The nature of the gods also comes with a weakness though, because if a god doesn't have at least one follower, it goes to the bottom of the well and stays there until eventually stops existing, or worse, becomes a human (according to Pareidolia). Regardless, not having followers offers them a fatal possibility.

The company comes in to facilitate and ensure both parts of the deal. For the gods, it ensures they'll suffer no risk of actual death, as the company can simply keep them under its employ. For the humans, it ensures their wishes won't go out of control or become something awful (monkey's paw thing), thus the caretakers, that come in every decade or two to perform repairs in a multitude of worlds.

Maya's world is extremely abnormal because the company isn't performing to protect the human (since Maya isn't one to begin with), and that it requires constant maintenance (resets aren't supposed to happen that often).

crustlord12 said:
Wanting to be a self insert in this game is all sorts of fucked up tbh. This is not a story about John Everyman, this is a story about Akira.
Click to expand...
Yeah, that goes without saying, I think. He is not supposed to be a character you can easily immerse yourself into.

The beginning, portraying itself mostly as a harem/VN parody with the MC having lost his memories, makes you think he is mostly a blank slate, but you learn about his character quite quickly and start to see him as a distinguished personality with thoughts, wants and values.

Compared to other games where MCs don't offer much of inner monologues and thoughts, sometimes not even letting the MC talk at all, this is merely a protagonist that you follow and through whose perspective you see the story unfold.

I know that in other games, like the one referenced in the original poster's signature banners, trying to identify yourself with the MC can work, but in those games MCs usually either don't have a strong character in the first place or it gives the player a lot of agency in shaping the story and MCs personality through active choices and branching.
This is no such game, and anyone not realizing that and wishing for it to become a story about themselves that they can immerse themselves into is going to have a bad time.

It's kind of like watching Pluribus and complaining that Carol is not just wishing for nude models to sleep with and getting infinite coke and finding out about the world's secrets (okay, that I probably would do as well). The show is not centered around fan service and living out a silly fantasy, it's trying to tell a story and the viewer is supposed to watch and understand the characters, not be them.
And the same basically applies to this game as well, Sensei is not supposed to be you. And frankly, if you identify a bit too much with him, you might need therapy
