View attachment 5493175
AND NOTHING!!! AHHHHH!!!

Don’t give me false hopes like that, okay! It’s horrible! She was two fingers away from revealing everything, then… no. Sensei was no longer interested!
Why are you asking, seeing that she’s ready to tell you everything, and you change your mind like that?! Asshole! Sacripant! Veule!

Sorry…


To lighten my mood, I’d like to touch on the Kirin/Haruka case. Strange as it may be, I really liked it (I sternly condemn what Haruka did, of course, but from a narrative standpoint, that passage was well-crafted).

But not Sana’s betrayal.
View attachment 5493170
I didn’t quite grasp it… she had a grievance against Kirin? I know Ayane did, but her? Even if Sana fantasizes about rape… she isn’t the one who’s raped (and she doesn’t even watch it!), so why?

No kidding, even now I wonder if it’s a «face-shifter» posing as her and triggering the following TPS. Seriously, I can’t explain it.

By the way, little aside, but the fact that Nao pulls Kirin out of her TPS with a slap… I don’t know. It’s both coherent and surprising.

Not to mention the shock when you wake up with that in front of you :
View attachment 5493169

Anyway, Kirin/Haruka, then. The scene was perfectly disturbing, and Haruka’s pathos was… truly pathetic. Yet, without absolving her actions, this scene with Chika :
View attachment 5493168
clearly shows the injustice of this world. Deep down, she’s right : why should Sensei get a pass (and be forgiven!), but not her?

Sure, she was much forceful than him (and to be fair, she HAS to initiate contact, whereas Sensei only has to pick up the slack). But beyond that, they’re both deviants.

And that’s why I even pray that the police catch her and arrest her. Already because it would illustrate Sensei’s impunity, and, more importantly, could potentially shift things up.

I’m worried, though, that her path is already set and she’s at high risk of joining the Yamaguchi clan.
Yeah. I’m serious. I have no proof of what I’m saying, but that’s what her character inspires me.

Also, to keep touching on Haruka a bit, the discussion with Maki and Sara perfectly illustrates why I don’t like talking to people:
View attachment 5493167
Maki expresses concern, not about the dress code, but about the reason behind that attire: to seduce Sensei.

Then she tells Haruka that she surely wouldn’t have a relationship with a child if he tried to seduce her, to which Haruka replies: «What if that were the case?»

Beyond Haruka’s provocation and Maki’s snap reaction, Sara defends Haruka, saying she’s trying to be civilized…


Really?


REALLY?!


Girl, did you follow the discussion? Hopefully, she connected the dot after finding Haruka in the bathroom (right after Kirin fled), and urge her to go home…

So, sure, we don’t see Sara’s facial expression (maybe she was pitying her...), but I sincerely hope there was disdain and reproach.
I won’t comment on the dialogue’s coherence, because, even if it gives me goosebumps, it seemed way too natural…



Let's keep the adults a bit longer and talk a little about Touka and Tsubasa, and I’ve got «one» little gripe :
View attachment 5493166

Strangely enough, maybe I’m misreading Touka’s character, but I’ve always seen her as smart and educated—especially on the political front. And there, her mother throws a purely political rhetoric, and she doesn’t even react! Even more, it’s the most worn-out rhetoric of all: «But why would we do that?»

At that moment I wanted to jump into the screen, slap Touka (she deserves it), and ask her mom: «And why wouldn’t you do it? What, morally, legally, TECHNICALLY, would stop you from doing it?»
Obviously I can’t do that (and even if I could, it wouldn’t have meant a thing), but hey… let me fantasize!


Now, let’s talk a bit about Chika/Rin, because… I think I fell in love with her. She’s far, far from my style… but this :
View attachment 5493165
Oh damn, I loved it! I was as surprised as Rin, actually. Okay, pleasantly surprised, but you get the idea. That drama!

I know I talk about it a lot, but God, I love it! That’s why I liked this update more than the previous one, by the way. Aside from the final «betrayal» of Himawari, there were no other moments that strong. In my view, at least.

Also, to stay a bit more on Chika, the moment right after she learns that her friend’s mother has cancer, with the narrator saying: «And she did what any other girl of her age would do.»

My first thought was: «Is she cutting her veins?»

And the answer was: «Run to the bathroom to cry even more.»

At that precise instant, I realized that my friends might not be normal… because, yes, their first reflex was to cut their veins… my childhood, and theirs, was the most joyful (sarcasm).


Now, Nodoka.

Nodoka was both a pleasant surprise and a slight disappointment.
We learn first that she remembers the goth girl who helps Himawari :
View attachment 5493159
Then that she’s «up-to-date» on the reset phenomenon:
View attachment 5493157
For me, that’s a missed opportunity.

But before I explain why, here’s how I picture people looping back to their last line when we bring up the reset thing:
Everyone has, or had, a «failsafe» in their heads that flips on the moment someone nearby talks about resets—kind of like a tape-player that, when the tape jams, pulls back just a tad to free itself.
But that «failsafe,» as I see it, is mechanical; it’s not about knowing the loop, but about the loop itself.
So the reason Makoto or Ayane recall the loop is simply that the system no longer works.

And that’s why I feel this is a missed chance: it would’ve been great for Nodoka to intellectually spot the loop, yet still be unable to articulate it plainly.
That would explain her cryptic way of talking about the loop all this time, and would show her «vulnerability»: she sees that the loop exists, but she’s still bound to it.
An intellectual tragedy that I’d have found epic… but nope.

And for the good surprise:
View attachment 5493156
Pure artistry.


And to wrap things up, Yasu God.
She makes it crystal-clear that Nozomu, who I still think is «HOPE,» is the creator of everything, all punctuated by «flashes» of Sensei being intimidated by his big brother Nozomu.

Is it a little presumptuous on my part to say that Sensei would be a god? I don’t think so, no. Especially with what Nodoka said earlier:
View attachment 5493154

Frankly, it would make sense. Yeah, it would also read like a Greek myth... and now that I think about it, I’m convinced a ton of parallels could be drawn. But that’ll be for another time (maybe).
Phew… ~1,600 words according to LibreOffice. It was long, but I wanted to write. And looking at my work, I hope I’m not on anyone’s blacklist! That would be a shame for them to miss this.

Anyway, that’s all from me...

Oh, I almost forgot, Ami, one last word?
View attachment 5493152
Sensei, I hate you, you know. She teases you and you don’t even notice.

And, finally… I vanish!
Click to expand...
A: Why is Maya's ass so fat.
B: Chika telling Haruka thats shes a predator was peak.
C: Sara protects Haruka in this conversation because she is 100% having a threesome with Akira and Sana. Shes in on it all now, she even knows Haruka is. She is protecting their point of view.
D: The character arc for Nodoka you say you want already happened, she DID figure out the time loop multiple times but was unable to grasp it, even asking Akira to stop her from looking into it, shes just now part of the club.

At that moment I wanted to jump into the screen, slap Touka (she deserves it), and ask her mom: «And why wouldn’t you do it? What, morally, legally, TECHNICALLY, would stop you from doing it?»
Obviously I can’t do that (and even if I could, it wouldn’t have meant a thing), but hey… let me fantasize!
Now, let’s talk a bit about Chika/Rin, because… I think I fell in love with her. She’s far, far from my style… but this :
Spoiler:
Confession
View attachment 5493165
Oh damn, I loved it! I was as surprised as Rin, actually. Okay, pleasantly surprised, but you get the idea. That drama!
I know I talk about it a lot, but God, I love it! That’s why I liked this update more than the previous one, by the way. Aside from the final «betrayal» of Himawari, there were no other moments that strong. In my view, at least.
Also, to stay a bit more on Chika, the moment right after she learns that her friend’s mother has cancer, with the narrator saying: «And she did what any other girl of her age would do.»
My first thought was: «Is she cutting her veins?»
And the answer was: «Run to the bathroom to cry even more.»
At that precise instant, I realized that my friends might not be normal… because, yes, their first reflex was to cut their veins… my childhood, and theirs, was the most joyful (sarcasm).
Now, Nodoka.
Nodoka was both a pleasant surprise and a slight disappointment.
We learn first that she remembers the goth girl who helps Himawari :
Spoiler:
So she remember
View attachment 5493159
Then that she’s «up-to-date» on the reset phenomenon:
Spoiler:
So she knows
View attachment 5493157
For me, that’s a missed opportunity.
But before I explain why, here’s how I picture people looping back to their last line when we bring up the reset thing:
Everyone has, or had, a «failsafe» in their heads that flips on the moment someone nearby talks about resets—kind of like a tape-player that, when the tape jams, pulls back just a tad to free itself.
But that «failsafe,» as I see it, is mechanical; it’s not about knowing the loop, but about the loop itself.
So the reason Makoto or Ayane recall the loop is simply that the system no longer works.
And that’s why I feel this is a missed chance: it would’ve been great for Nodoka to intellectually spot the loop, yet still be unable to articulate it plainly.
That would explain her cryptic way of talking about the loop all this time, and would show her «vulnerability»: she sees that the loop exists, but she’s still bound to it.
An intellectual tragedy that I’d have found epic… but nope.
And for the good surprise:
Spoiler:
Mother?
View attachment 5493156
Pure artistry.
And to wrap things up,
Yasu
God.
She makes it crystal-clear that Nozomu, who I still think is «HOPE,» is the creator of everything, all punctuated by «flashes» of Sensei being intimidated by his big brother Nozomu.
Is it a little presumptuous on my part to say that Sensei would be a god? I don’t think so, no. Especially with what Nodoka said earlier:
Spoiler:
Become a gods
View attachment 5493154
Frankly, it would make sense. Yeah, it would also read like a Greek myth... and now that I think about it, I’m convinced a ton of parallels could be drawn. But that’ll be for another time (maybe).

I'm not arguing that Makoto's feelings here aren't understandable from her perspective, I was mostly just trying to point out that her perspective has been coloured by extreme circumstances - and also that I don't think some of those circumstances necessarily change things in this instance as much as she thinks they do.
Click to expand...
The point that you've been making for pages is that a mother is right in worrying that teenagers are actively trying to seduce their teacher. That this isn't healthy to either part, and that you can't understand why so many people think that Maki is wrong in saying this - and, by extension, that Makoto is wrong based on the manner by which she responds.

Aside from that, I don't know how to take the notion that "I wouldn't address your point". I have been replying in good faith. But since you also edited that out, I'll ignore that statement.

I do believe my in-depth analysis addresses your point fully. But if even that isn't enough, I'll say that no one will dispute you on the very general idea that teenagers shouldn't seduce teachers, and vice-versa. But to dissect a scene, I think we ought to consider who is saying what to whom, how they're saying it, and the general point of the scene.

Maki's scene, from a story standpoint, was never about any of what she says. It was about finding out that your daughter's teacher (and close friend/lover) is a traumatized pedophile, and then being unable to deal with things in a reasonable manner because only she (to her knowledge) is privy to this information. So, while everything gets a new connotation for her, she just sounds like an insane person to everyone else - while being unable to properly convey why she now has a problem with everything she didn't have a problem before.

Selebus' choice on having her constantly worry about girls dressing slutty, when the only one dressed slutty is her - is to highlight this point. Why not have Maki worry about an actual problem? Well, because then she wouldn't sound insane.

I also don't get what is it exactly on Makoto's reaction that seems unearned to you. She does correct Maki's grammar, but that's just as Maki keeps making sex jokes (this is not a reaction to her argument, just their dynamic). Maki replies back with teasing about Makoto feeling superior by correcting her, and Makoto replies that she's the one trying to feel superior by telling her how to behave sexually, when she most certainly didn't display this knowledge raising her. Which is also to the point. This isn't a response to the idea that "the girls shouldn't seduce Akira", this is a response to the fact that Maki's behaving in a way she normally wouldn't.

This trend continues as Maki says she's worried the girls are dressed slutty. Makoto points out that the only one dressed slutty is Maki, and that it's not the girl's purpose to restrict themselves on a male's behalf. Maki says she's just worried for them, Makoto replies that it makes no sense, especially that she's saying all of this to Makoto. These are all appropriate responses to the topic at hand, and doubly so. Because Maki has never had a problem with it thus far, and is behaving like a lunatic for reasons that, as we've established, only make sense to her.

By the way, Makoto never says Maki is wrong. In fact, Maki is the one that proposes she's wrong, and Makoto denies her. Instead saying that no one disagreed with her, just that she's looking to a situation without nuance.

Anyway, I'm open if you want to clarify something I still don't understand. But that's also fine if you'd just rather let it rest.

spoilers.html:
The point that you've been making for pages is that a mother is right in worrying that teenagers are actively trying to seduce their teacher. That this isn't healthy to either part, and that you can't understand why so many people think that Maki is wrong in saying this - and, by extension, that Makoto is wrong based on the manner by which she responds.

Aside from that, I don't know how to take the notion that "I wouldn't address your point". I have been replying in good faith. But since you also edited that out, I'll ignore that statement.

I do believe my in-depth analysis addresses your point fully. But if even that isn't enough, I'll say that no one will dispute you on the very general idea that teenagers shouldn't seduce teachers, and vice-versa. But to dissect a scene, I think we ought to consider who is saying what to whom, how they're saying it, and the general point of the scene.

Maki's scene, from a story standpoint, was never about any of what she says. It was about finding out that your daughter's teacher (and close friend/lover) is a traumatized pedophile, and then being unable to deal with things in a reasonable manner because only she (to her knowledge) is privy to this information. So, while everything gets a new connotation for her, she just sounds like an insane person to everyone else - while being unable to properly convey why she now has a problem with everything she didn't have a problem before.

Selebus' choice on having her constantly worry about girls dressing slutty, when the only one dressed slutty is her - is to highlight this point. Why not have Maki worry about an actual problem? Well, because then she wouldn't sound insane.

If I wanted a VN that hits the same as Lessons In Love - or close to it - could anyone suggest one?
Click to expand...
Well, I think there's Dissonance and Sorrow of Rebirth.
As mentioned by others, the former is very SoL and slow burn, and Toru isn't really self-hating like Sensei, though the game has, I believe a small dash of mystery to its denpa. Also, from what I skimmed, it may share some similarities in endgame plot with Out of Touch (haven't played this one, though it seems more classical VN than kinetic like LiL and its associates).
For the latter, it's really rough and short compared to the other two, it's on its second "reset", to use LiL comparisons even if inaccurate (though in length it may seem to be just the first one) but I liked Shiba enough to offset how much the MC really feels like a tool sometimes (even if that may be a plot point considering his niece).

John Smith V said:
I might have to review 0.53.0 - seems I didnt internalize enough of what was presented. Pretty sure I missed things as they relate to Maya.
Click to expand...
In case you are still lost even after re-reading it, the mechanics haven't been really explained, but you can get a fair bit from what the wish world is and the small in-game explanation.
Have you heard of the anthropic principle? I think the wish worlds work like that, a simulation based on the observer that will keep running for said observer while patching up stuff in the background. Only that, since it's Himawari's world, Sensei's and Ayane's existence and agency start to glitch it, which is what I think Sana and Ami are.
Kinda like how the world in Parahumans makes just enough sense to work from the eyes of its vict-protagonist, but is held by a thread outside of it (and yes, I'm including the in-story deii ex machina).
This, if I understand correctly, is why Maya, who is herself a wish, managing to make a wish world is seen as such an anomaly, the system SHOULDN'T work like that. Also, I'm like 50% certain that one world where Ami penetrated Nodoka hard and fast was Sekai's wish world.

john doeer said:
I've been curious about doing a good uncle run, do events like the Nodokathon still take place just without the Ami part? Or are scenes like that missed entirely?
Click to expand...
Nodokathon 2 is cut in half and you get a note from Ayane instead of like 4 events. By far, not sleeping with Ami cuts you out of most events out of any choice. Many of them barely having to do with Ami. It also screws continuity tbh.

After her, iirc, not sleeping with Sara will cut about 2-3 Himawari scenes. Other than those, things are more or less restricted to the missed person's arc. I'm talking about full events so far, not variations.

Do mind though that it has been a trend to couple red path choices together, so chances are that people will keep missing every possible event that can be missed soon enough.

Also, being real rn, Selebus himself said that it was a mistake to make a red path at all apart from the Ami choice. But given his poor implementation of "good uncle" I'd argue against even that. It feels like you're reading a book and then skipping whole chapters because you don't like a specific character.

Edit: regarding the post above, "you, me and her" requires an iron stomach to read. Fucked up shit.
